items.title: Journalisme africain : Dakar accueille les 23 et 24 novembre une conférence sur le modèle économique des médias
items.description: Organisée par la Convention des Jeunes Reporters du Sénégal avec la Fondation Konrad Adenauer, la Conférence des jeunes journalistes africains se tiendra les 23 et 24 novembre 2026 à Dakar. La rencontre veut trouver comment financer une presse libre en Afrique. Comment un média peut-il vivre sans perdre sa liberté ? La question sera au centre de la Conférence des jeunes journalistes africains, qui se tiendra à Dakar les 23 et 24 novembre 2026. Cette rencontre continentale réunira des professionnels des médias autour d'un défi : trouver des modèles économiques capables de garantir l'indépendance et la pérennité du journalisme sur le continent. La conférence est portée par la Convention des Jeunes Reporters du Sénégal (CJRS), en partenariat avec la Fondation Konrad Adenauer. Elle se tiendra sous le thème « Quel modèle économique pour un journalisme indépendant ? ». Les organisateurs veulent en faire un cadre de dialogue, de réflexion et de partage d'expériences entre jeunes professionnels africains. Un secteur sous pression L'événement arrive à un moment délicat pour la presse africaine. Les organisateurs décrivent un paysage médiatique traversé par de « profondes mutations » et énumèrent les difficultés : situation financière fragile des entreprises de presse, transformation numérique, recul des revenus publicitaires, évolution des habitudes de consommation de l'information et arrivée de nouveaux acteurs. Ces défis, estiment-ils, obligent les médias à repenser leurs modèles de fonctionnement et de financement. Les échanges porteront en particulier sur l'indépendance éditoriale, que le communiqué lie à la capacité des rédactions de mobiliser des ressources « durables et diversifiées ». Les participants chercheront des pistes pour que les médias préservent leur liberté de ton, leur crédibilité et leur rôle dans la vie démocratique. La conférence se veut aussi un espace de réseautage et de coopération. Selon les organisateurs, elle favorisera le partage de bonnes pratiques et la circulation des expériences, avec l'espoir de voir naître de nouvelles initiatives « en faveur d'un journalisme plus résilient ». L'ambition de la CJRS Par cette initiative, la CJRS dit vouloir contribuer à l'émergence d'une génération de journalistes mieux armés face aux bouleversements du secteur. Elle espère aussi participer à la construction d'un écosystème médiatique africain « plus solide, pluraliste et indépendant ». Pendant deux jours, Dakar sera ainsi le lieu où des jeunes journalistes du continent chercheront des modèles économiques viables au service d'une information libre, crédible et durable.

items.title: Man’s penis reattached at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital after accident
items.description: Surgeons at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital have successfully reattached a man’s severed penis in a rare and complex procedure, the hospital’s Board Chair, Professor Titus Beyuo, has disclosed. The operation was performed by specialists at the hospital’s Urology and Nephrology Centre after the patient reportedly slipped while attempting to sit on a water closet (WC), resulting in the severing of his penis. Speaking on Accra-based Channel One TV on Saturday, November 21, Professor Beyuo described the procedure as a significant medical achievement, saying the surgical team had successfully reattached the organ and restored its function. “Korle Bu has been in the news for good and mixed reasons this past week but we have very good news to announce today where our team of surgeons at the urology and nephology center, have successfully reimplanted a severed penis of a man. “The person was attempting to sit on a WC and slipped and it was cut off. The good news is that our team of doctors has completely and successfully reattached it and it is functioning. There are rare cases of this in the medical literature and I think it is something good to celebrate.” Professor Beyuo commended the surgeons and other medical professionals involved, describing the outcome as a successful intervention. He said cases of this nature were rare in medical literature, making the achievement particularly noteworthy.

items.title: ‘Give us back our school’ – Mfantsipim Old Boys appeal to government
items.description: The Mfantsipim Old Boys Association (MOBA) has called on the government to reconsider the management structure of Mfantsipim School and allow the association to assume greater responsibility for its development through a restructured partnership with the state and the Methodist Church. The association’s 5th Ebusuapanyin, Moses Kwesi Baiden Jnr, made the appeal during the school’s 150th anniversary celebration at Kwabotwe Hill in Cape Coast, calling for a new institutional framework that would give the school greater flexibility in its operations, financing and governance. Addressing Vice President Prof. Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang and other dignitaries at the ceremony, he said MOBA was proposing a feasibility study into a not-for-profit partnership that would preserve public access to the school while strengthening its capacity to deliver quality education. “Please give us back our school,” he appealed. He explained that the proposal was not intended to turn Mfantsipim into a private institution or relieve the government of its responsibilities, but to empower the association to share greater responsibility for the school’s development under an accountable arrangement. Mr Baiden Jnr said the proposed framework should establish clear responsibilities for the government, the Methodist Church, MOBA and other stakeholders, with transparent financial arrangements, independent oversight and measurable educational outcomes. He also suggested that the model could explore how government support, alumni endowments, philanthropy and other lawful contributions could be mobilised to improve teaching, laboratories, digital infrastructure, boarding facilities, teacher development and scholarships. He stressed that any new arrangement must protect access for students from less privileged backgrounds, insisting that financial circumstances should not prevent academically qualified students from attending the school. “A new model must never become a clever way of reserving excellence for the wealthy,” he said. The MOBA leader proposed that Mfantsipim be considered as a pilot for the arrangement, subject to the outcome of the feasibility study and agreement among the relevant authorities. He cited Nigeria’s partnership involving the Federal Government and the King’s College Old Boys’ Association in Lagos as an example of an arrangement worth examining, although he cautioned that Ghana should develop a model suited to its own educational and institutional circumstances. Mr Baiden Jnr said the proposal was driven by the need to secure the school’s future beyond its 150th anniversary, arguing that preserving its history and infrastructure alone would not guarantee its continued relevance. The Ebusuapanyin also disclosed that MOBA and other non-governmental contributors had committed approximately GH¢150 million towards infrastructure development and anniversary-related projects. He said the investment was intended to improve facilities such as classrooms, laboratories, sports infrastructure and boarding facilities. He also cited government support of approximately GH¢4 million for the school in 2026, stressing the importance of recognising the contributions of all stakeholders. Mr Baiden Jnr further announced plans to establish a US$10 million endowment fund to support Mfantsipim’s long-term development, saying the initiative would commence immediately after the anniversary celebrations. He said MOBA USA’s endowment initiative was approaching US$300,000, while MOBA Foundation UK had raised funds to support science education at the school. Reflecting on the school’s 150-year history, Mr Baiden Jnr said Mfantsipim had endured because successive generations of old boys and other stakeholders had taken responsibility for its survival and development. He recalled the school’s establishment in 1876 as Wesleyan High School in Cape Coast with 17 boys, describing its history as one of institutional resilience, African initiative and a commitment to education. He said the institution’s contribution to Ghana extended beyond academic achievements, citing the role of its alumni in law, public administration, diplomacy, science, business, the arts and national development. He also called for a renewed focus on the quality and relevance of secondary education, arguing that academic excellence must go beyond examination results to equip students with critical thinking, technological skills, creativity, integrity and a sense of national responsibility. “Examinations matter, but a nation cannot be transformed by examination passes alone,” he said. Mr Baiden Jnr urged the government, the Methodist Church, MOBA, teachers, parents and students to work together to strengthen the institution and prepare it for the next 150 years. Mfantsipim School, established on April 3, 1876, is marking its 150th anniversary in 2026 under the leadership of its old boys’ association and other stakeholders.

items.title: At SCO moot in India, Musadik Malik declares climate change ‘enemy’ of civilisations
items.description: Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik on Saturday declared climate change an “enemy” of civilisations as he highlighted its impact on South Asian countries at a meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in India. Malik is in New Delhi on a three-day trip to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, making him the first Pakistani minister to visit the neighbour since former foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari attended an SCO meeting in May 2023. Addressing the forum on Saturday, the minister said the enemy of this civilisation was not another civilisation but climate change, noting that Nepal’s representative also spoke about the issue. Malik recalled the Aug 26 floods in Nepal, which claimed over 1,400 lives and left thousands of others missing, as well as the devastating 2022 floods in Pakistan. He noted that those monsoon floods left 1,700 people dead and submerged one-third of the country, including almost the entire Sindh. “Four days of rain caused Mohenjo Daro’s walls to fall; those walls that no one was able to break for 4,500 years, climate [change] and rain-induced floods did it.” The minister remarked that humans were also an “enemy”, as they contributed to climate destruction. “Do you know what is the meaning of Mohenjo-Daro?” Malik asked. “It means mound of the dead.” Malik said the ancient site had, in a sense, opened its gates to the living during the 2022 floods, providing refuge to people displaced by the disaster. He said people had sought shelter wherever they could find it, including parking lots and shopping malls, while mosques, temples, shrines and schools in Balochistan had also opened their doors to those affected by the floods. “This is the power of civilisation. This is the power through which nations survive,” the minister noted. During his speech, Malik presented three proposals for SCO, including the establishment of a network of cultural institutions, a digital repository to present the region’s historical and natural “gifts” to the world, and a climate-resilient heritage framework to address destruction caused by climate change in the region. At the outset of his address, Malik said he had initially intended to deliver his speech in English but felt more inclined to speak in Urdu after considering his proximity to the tombs of Urdu poet Mirza Ghalib and Sufi saint Nizamuddin. “It felt a little strange to speak in English. So, with your permission, I would like to speak in Urdu,” he said. The minister pointed out that distinct identities were needed for dialogue, which could only take place between diverse voices. “If there is one identity, one voice, then a monologue is needed. There is no need for dialogue,” he said, comparing it to waking up in the morning, looking in the mirror and speaking only to oneself. “There is no beauty in that. Beauty is [in] the vase that has colourful flowers, the smell of different kinds. Today, we’re here to celebrate that colourful vase,” the minister said. During his address, the minister highlighted Pakistan’s history and how its civilisation had been shaped by multiple influences, with connections extending across China, Central Asia, Iran and the Middle East. “When we look at our history, all our roads lead to the north; Bukhara and Samarkand and Central Asia and Afghanistan. The entire history takes us to the north,” he said. “And when we talk about our prayers, our poetry, we are drawn towards the Middle East and Iran or Persia.” Malik said diversity and the free flow of ideas and identities were something to be embraced. “There is wisdom there, in embracing it. We’re here to celebrate these things today.” Meetings with Indian minister, others Dr Malik arrived at Purana Qila in New Delhi for the second day of the inaugural SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, according to a post shared by his office earlier in the day. On the sidelines of the forum, Malik held separate bilateral meetings with representatives from various countries, including host India, Nepal, Iran and Tajikistan. He met with Indian Minister for Culture and Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat and Indian Secretary for Culture Vivek Aggarwal, state-run APP reported. According to APP , the discussions focused on cultural ties and opportunities for promoting cooperation between Pakistan and India, with both sides exchanging views on matters of mutual interest and the importance of strengthening cultural and civilisational links. During his meeting with Nepal’s Culture and Tourism Minister Khadga Raj Poudel, the climate change minister expressed deep grief over the loss of precious human lives in the August floods. Malik emphasised that urgent global action was essential to address the growing risks of natural disasters caused by climate change. In his meeting with Tajikistan’s Minister of Culture Sattoriyon Amonzoda, Malik underscored the strong historical and cultural ties between the two countries, the Pakistan High Commission in India said. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s resolve to further strengthen these multifaceted ties, particularly through greater people-to-people exchanges. In a separate meeting with the president of Iran’s Islamic Culture and Relations Organisation, Mohammad Mahdi Imanipour, Dr Malik underscored the deep-rooted historical and cultural bonds between Pakistan and Iran. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s firm commitment to further expanding these fraternal ties across all spheres, the high commission said. Meanwhile, Malik and Azerbaijan’s Culture Minister Adil Karimli expressed their commitment to further strengthening the long-standing fraternal ties between Islamabad and Baku. Malik emphasised the need to enhance cooperation across all sectors of the bilateral relationship between the two countries. The climate change minister also met with Kyrgyz Republic’s Deputy Minister of Culture and Youth Policy Askaraly Shukuralievich. A day earlier, after arriving in New Delhi, Malik had described the forum as a “tremendous opportunity” for multilateral dialogue, saying that cultures and civilisations transcended geographical boundaries. Speaking to Indian news agency ANI , he had said the gathering offered an opportunity to discuss shared history, geography, cultures and civilisations. Malik’s India trip comes two years after India’s External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar visited Islamabad for an SCO meeting. Pakistan currently holds the rotating chairmanship of the SCO Council of Heads of State for the 2026-27 term and is scheduled to host the organisation’s summit in Islamabad in August 2027.

items.title: Makinde’s image on campaign balloon stirs controversy at Tinubu’s Ibadan rally
items.description: By Adeola Badru The image of Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, displayed alongside those of President Bola Tinubu and other political figures on a balloon hoisted at the venue of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ibadan on Saturday has stirred reactions, drawing attention to the governor’s political stance ahead of the 2027 general elections. The balloon, which was hoisted at the rally ground around the historic Mapo Hall, featured the images of prominent political figures, including Makinde, who is not a member of the APC and has yet to publicly declare support for Tinubu’s re-election bid. The development attracted attention at the campaign venue, where the President was expected to rally support for the APC and its candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. Makinde, who is the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), has been at the centre of political discussions in Oyo State following his emergence as the party’s flag bearer. His image on the balloon, therefore, raised questions about the message being conveyed by its display at an APC campaign rally, particularly as the political atmosphere in the state continues to intensify ahead of the next general election. The circumstances surrounding the inclusion of the governor’s image on the balloon were not immediately clear as at the time of filing this report. Meanwhile, President Tinubu has urged the people of Oyo State to sustain their support for the APC, declaring that continuity was essential for Nigeria’s progress, prosperity and development. Tinubu, who spoke at the rally, promised increased investment in education, agriculture, industrialisation and electricity supply, while endorsing Senator Sharafadeen Alli as the APC’s governorship candidate in the state. The President also announced plans to revive the old Leyland factory in Ibadan, saying his administration had signed an agreement with Chinese company Yutong to reopen the facility for the production of public transport vehicles and the establishment of an automobile assembly plant. “For Oyo State, we have just signed an agreement with China’s Yutong to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport vehicles and establish an automobile assembly plant there. We will continue to bring industries. You will see progress and development,” Tinubu said. He also assured residents of improved electricity supply, expressing confidence in the efforts of the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, and his team. “You will see, and I guarantee you an improvement in electricity. Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe is really working hard with his team,” he said. Tinubu urged the electorate to remain committed to the APC, reminding them of their support for the party in the previous election. “You voted overwhelmingly for APC last time. You must stay the course. You must. For the sake of progress, prosperity of our country, development, for your children and our great-grandchildren,” he said. The President added that the country must prioritise education and agriculture to create opportunities for younger generations. “We must give them the right education, invest in agriculture,” he said. He also took a swipe at opposition parties, describing them as “mediocre”, and urged the electorate not to be distracted by them. Tinubu subsequently declared his support for Alli, urging the people of Oyo State to vote for him in the 2027 governorship election. “I will show you the governorship candidate in Oyo State that you must vote for, and is Sen. Sharafadeen Alli,” he said. The rally was preceded by the arrival of the President at the Ladoke Akintola Airport, Ibadan, where the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, and other traditional rulers received him. The monarchs, drawn from the Ibadan, Ibarapa, Oyo, Ogbomoso and Oke-Ogun zones, reaffirmed their support for Tinubu’s re-election bid. Welcoming the President on behalf of the Oyo State Council of Obas and Chiefs, Ladoja described Tinubu as the leader the monarchs had been waiting to receive. “This is the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu that we have been waiting for,” the Olubadan said. The monarch commended the President for infrastructure projects across the country, particularly in the South-West, including the Leyland Motor Assembly project, the Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode Road and the Ibadan-Oyo Road. He, however, urged that ongoing projects be completed before fresh requests were made for additional ones. Tinubu thanked the monarchs for their prayers and co-operation, urging them to encourage their subjects to participate in the forthcoming election. The President also called for a minute’s silence in honour of those who lost their lives in a boat accident in Bayelsa State, expressing sympathy with the bereaved families. Earlier, chaos had broken out at the rally venue as hoodlums clashed before the President’s arrival, with gunshots fired into the air. The incident caused panic among supporters, who scampered for safety as the situation deteriorated. Some of the hoodlums were seen dragging a firearm reportedly used by an unidentified man, while others hurled sticks and placards towards the media stand, disrupting activities at the venue. The scuffle dispersed parts of the crowd and briefly disrupted preparations for the President’s arrival. The post Makinde’s image on campaign balloon stirs controversy at Tinubu’s Ibadan rally appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: REC confirms 2.8m registered voters in Edo
items.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – THE Edo State Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), Obo Effanga yest said that the state currently has 2.8 million registered voters. According to him, the last registration exercise raised the figure adding that the final figure would be released after the recent clean up exercise by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Giving an update on the Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) collection in Benin City, Effanga said a total of 23,401 cards had been collected across the state since distribution commenced on October 9. He explained that the figure comprised 6,319 old PVCs, 5,128 newly produced cards and 11,954 PVCs relating to transfers. Effanga noted, “The state currently has 2.8 million registered voters after the last registration exercise. However, the final figure would be released after the recent clean up exercise by the national body.” The REC disclosed that PVCs for voters who registered during the first and second phases of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise were currently available for collection at INEC offices across the 18 local government areas of the state. The Resident Commissioner said the commission was currently working towards ensuring a smooth electoral process. Speaking on the mock accreditation exercise scheduled for November 28, the REC said the exercise would be conducted in 384 polling units across the state. He said two polling units were selected from each of the 192 wards also known as registration areas for the mock exercise. “The exercise would provide an opportunity to test the commission’s electoral technology and assess the readiness of its personnel ahead of the elections. “The state office had submitted the list of proposed polling units to the commission’s headquarters for approval,” he added. He said the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System would be deployed during the exercise to demonstrate how voters are accredited, how results are captured and how they are transmitted to the INEC Result Viewing Portal. items.title: Jonathan: Nigeria needs honest leaders to restore global respect
items.description: …Ex-President condemns money-driven politics, primitive wealth accumulation …Says democracy has standards, calls for investment in younger generation By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called for purposeful, honest and visionary political leadership to rebuild Nigeria’s battered international image and restore the respect the country once commanded globally. Jonathan, who spoke at the Paul Alaje Colloquium, themed “The Nigeria Brand”, in Abuja yesterday, said the country needed leaders who were deliberate about national development rather than personal wealth accumulation. He lamented that the quality of politics currently practised in Nigeria was undermining democracy and threatening the country’s progress. “Some of what goes on in our political space does not represent democracy. The brand of politics we are playing will set us backwards. Democracy has standards,” he said. The former president criticised politicians who lacked knowledge of their parties’ manifestos, noting that many of the documents were prepared by hired consultants without any meaningful commitment from the candidates. He urged political leaders to emulate the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo, whose clear vision and commitment to compulsory education transformed the old Western Region. According to Jonathan, Awolowo’s education policy produced remarkable results, with the South-West at a point having more professors than the rest of Nigeria combined. He challenged present-day leaders to abandon primitive accumulation of wealth and invest in the younger generation, stressing that leadership should be measured by the legacy left behind. “Why will you stomach what you are supposed to invest in the younger generation at a time you know your time on earth is really not much?” he asked. Speaking on the importance of a strong national identity, Jonathan said a country’s brand went beyond public relations, reflecting its character, leadership, institutions and development aspirations. “A strong national brand attracts investment, tourism, international partnerships and opportunities for its citizens. It inspires patriotism at home and commands respect abroad. “Therefore, discussing the Nigeria brand is not an exercise in public relations. It is a conversation about national character, leadership, development and the kind of country we want to leave to our children,” he said. Jonathan recalled that Nigeria once enjoyed considerable international respect and influence but regretted that its reputation had suffered significant setbacks. He identified insecurity, corruption, economic difficulties, unemployment, political instability and negative perceptions of public institutions as factors damaging the country’s image. The former president particularly expressed concern over the limited international mobility associated with the Nigerian passport, which exposes citizens to considerable visa restrictions and difficulties travelling abroad. However, he cautioned against equating the country’s challenges with the character of its people, maintaining that millions of Nigerians remained honest, industrious, talented and respected internationally. He attributed the deterioration of Nigeria’s national identity partly to the erosion of societal values, where wealth was celebrated without questions about its source, while honesty, hard work and integrity received insufficient recognition. Other factors, he said, included corruption, abuse of public office, impunity, weakened public institutions and insecurity, which had created doubts about the ability of the state to guarantee the safety of lives and property. To reverse the trend, Jonathan called for stronger leadership and governance, insisting that public office must be treated as a position of trust. He said merit, competence, transparency, accountability and the rule of law must become the guiding principles of public administration. He also advocated reforms in political recruitment, stronger internal party democracy, credible elections and a political culture that rewards ideas, character and competence rather than money, patronage and sectional interests. In his remarks, the convener of the colloquium, Dr. Paul Alaje, challenged Nigerians to examine the country’s international reputation by considering whether the world could trust Nigeria enough to invest in it and entrust its resources and future to its institutions. He said the Nigeria brand was fundamentally about the country’s institutions and what they represented. Alaje identified a troubling paradox in Nigeria’s development, noting that despite its enormous human capital and global achievements in music, film, literature, technology, medicine, finance, academia and engineering, the country continued to struggle with basic human development indicators. He questioned how a country blessed with enormous human capital could struggle with human development, abundant agricultural potential yet find it difficult to feed its population, and a vibrant entrepreneurial spirit without an enabling business environment. According to him, Nigeria must stop confusing potential with progress and deliberately address the structural challenges holding it back. He cited China, India and South Africa as countries that had worked to change their international narratives, arguing that Nigeria could achieve similar results through deliberate policies and consistent implementation. Alaje expressed concern over Nigeria’s poor life expectancy and widespread poverty, saying the country needed to become intentional about improving the living conditions of its citizens. He called for policies that would encourage domestic production of goods for local consumption and export, while urging state governments to collaborate with the federal government and private-sector operators to expand electricity supply under the new electricity regulatory framework. He also advocated productivity-enhancing policies in agriculture, more efficient transportation systems and increased investment in health and education as critical measures for raising living standards and rebuilding confidence in Nigeria. The post Jonathan: Nigeria needs honest leaders to restore global respect appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Littérature : à 16 ans, Adama Kadé Touré présente ses nouveaux ouvrages et invite la jeunesse guinéenne à prendre la plume
items.description: A seulement 16 ans, Adama Kadé Touré poursuit son ascension dans l’univers littéraire guinéen. Écrivaine et ambassadrice de Conakry, ville créative de l’UNESCO dans le domaine de la littérature, la jeune auteure a présenté et dédicacé ses ouvrages ce samedi 21 novembre, à Conakry. Une rencontre au cours de laquelle elle a partagé son parcours, ses inspirations et sa vision de l’écriture, tout en lançant un appel à la jeunesse à lire, à écrire et à croire en ses rêves. Partie de l’écriture à l’âge de 11 ans, Adama Kadé Touré a publié son premier ouvrage, L’Encre du destin, alors qu’elle n’avait que 14 ans. Aujourd’hui, elle compte trois livres à son actif : L’Encre du destin, Afrique, ta jeunesse t’écrit, et L’Empire des brisés. Pour la jeune écrivaine, cette dédicace représente une nouvelle étape d’un parcours entamé avec beaucoup de curiosité, de rêves et une profonde envie de raconter des histoires. « À cet âge, j’avais surtout des rêves, beaucoup de curiosité et l’envie de raconter des histoires. Je ne savais pas où cette aventure me conduirait aujourd’hui », a-t-elle confié, avant de rappeler que son écriture et sa manière de comprendre le rôle du livre dans la société ont considérablement évolué depuis ses débuts. « Aujourd’hui, à mes seize ans, je mesure ce chemin avec reconnaissance et je sais qu’il reste énormément à apprendre », a-t-elle ajouté. « Afrique, ta jeunesse t’écrit », un livre miroir pour la jeunesse Parmi les ouvrages présentés, « Afrique, ta jeunesse t’écrit » occupe une place particulière dans la démarche littéraire de la jeune auteure. Né d’une réflexion sur la place accordée à la jeunesse africaine dans les débats qui la concernent, ce livre se veut un espace d’expression, de réflexion et de construction personnelle. « Nous parlons beaucoup de ma génération, cette jeunesse africaine confrontée entre défis et perspectives. Mais est-ce qu’on nous laisse suffisamment d’espace pour nous exprimer et pour penser ? », s’est interrogée Adama Kadé Touré. À travers cet ouvrage, elle souhaite permettre aux jeunes de se reconnaître dans les réalités évoquées, de réfléchir à leur environnement et de construire leur propre regard sur le monde. L’auteure le présente comme un « livre miroir », organisé en quatre parties : « Ma vision », « Nos réalités », « Ce que je veux dire à nous, la jeunesse » et « À toi maintenant ». Mais au-delà de sa génération, Adama Kadé Touré souhaite également que les adultes, les parents et les responsables de la société s’intéressent à cet ouvrage, afin de mieux comprendre les préoccupations quotidiennes des jeunes. « Celui-ci, certes, je l’ai écrit pour que ce soit un espace d’expression pour ma génération, mais je voudrais aussi que vous, les hommes de maintenant, nos adultes, nos parents, vous puissiez le lire pour mieux comprendre ce que nous vivons au quotidien », a-t-elle lancé. L’Empire des brisés, un hommage à Forécariah et à ses communautés L’autre ouvrage présenté lors de cette rencontre, « L’Empire des brisés » plonge le lecteur dans un univers fictif inspiré de la Basse-Côte guinéenne. À travers ce roman, la jeune écrivaine a voulu faire un clin d’œil à sa ville natale, Forécariah, en situant l’histoire dans un royaume appelé Foré. « Foré, Forécariah, un jeu de mots », a-t-elle expliqué, précisant que, même si l’histoire est fictive, elle espère que les lecteurs originaires de cette localité pourront y retrouver des fragments de leur histoire et de leur environnement. L’univers du roman se dévoile dès les premières lignes, dans une description évocatrice du royaume : « Le soir étendait lentement son manteau sur le royaume de Foré. Le ciel, encore ourlé de nuages orange et violette, se chargeait peu à peu d’ombre épaisse. Un vent lourd, tiède et chargé de poussière rouge, venait de caresser les toits de chaume et soulevait des tourbillons au cœur de la grande place du village ». Dans ce récit, Adama Kadé Touré met en avant le destin de N’na Gallé, une femme belle, courageuse et intelligente, admirée par son entourage. Mais, comme elle le souligne, dans certaines communautés, ceux qui brillent trop fortement peuvent devenir la cible de la jalousie et du mauvais œil. La destinée de cette femme se poursuit à travers son enfant, N’Dakhi, qui entreprend de redorer sa mémoire et de faire en sorte que les personnes brisées par la société et leurs communautés puissent trouver un refuge. « Mais comme il n’y a jamais de fin totale pour une étoile, il reste toujours des étincelles », a-t-elle résumé, évoquant cette lumière qui subsiste malgré les épreuves. À travers « L’Empire des brisés », l’auteure entend également transmettre des valeurs et faire découvrir certaines réalités culturelles. Elle reconnaît ne pas avoir grandi pleinement au contact des traditions de sa communauté, mais explique s’être inspirée de celles-ci pour apprendre et nourrir son imagination. « Lorsque vous toucherez mon roman, ou même plutôt mes romans, je voudrais d’abord que les gens comprennent à quel point l’écriture est un moyen de transmission », a-t-elle déclaré. Une jeune auteure déjà présente sur la scène littéraire africaine Au-delà de ses publications, Adama Kadé Touré s’est progressivement fait une place dans le paysage littéraire, en Guinée comme à l’extérieur du pays. Plusieurs fois lauréate du Prix africain jeune littéraire, elle a également été finaliste du Prix littéraire des lycéens de Guinée en 2025. Elle est ambassadrice de Conakry, ville créative de l’UNESCO dans le domaine de la littérature, et représentante en Guinée de l’Organisation littéraire sans frontières. Son parcours l’a conduite à participer à plusieurs rendez-vous littéraires africains, notamment au Salon du livre féminin de Dakar, à la Foire internationale du livre de Ouagadougou, au Marché du livre et des arts du Nigeria, au Festival international du livre et des arts gabonais, ainsi qu’au Festival du livre et des arts assimilés du Bénin. Pour la jeune écrivaine, cette ouverture sur le continent s’explique par une inspiration puisée dans son environnement immédiat. « Mon inspiration vient de partout, de tout ce qui est vivant autour de moi, de ma communauté et surtout de la Guinée », a-t-elle affirmé. Elle rappelle également que son aventure littéraire a commencé par la lecture, qu’elle considère comme le fondement de son parcours. « Je suis une très grande lectrice avant tout, avant d’être écrivaine. C’est le livre qui m’a amenée à l’écrit », a-t-elle souligné. L’Association des écrivains de Guinée encourage la relève Présent à cette rencontre, le président de l’Association des écrivains de Guinée a exprimé la satisfaction de son organisation de prendre part à cette cérémonie consacrée à la jeune auteure. S’adressant aux jeunes présents, il les a invités à s’inspirer de l’exemple de leurs camarades qui ont réussi à franchir les étapes de la création littéraire. « Nos autrices-là sont vos camarades, vos petites sœurs, vos grandes sœurs certainement pour certains. Mais s’il vous plaît, l’imitation, la bonne imitation… Quand on dit “on n’imite personne servant de modèle aux autres”, mais la bonne imitation vient d’en haut et d’en haut, ce sont vos sœurs-là qui vous ont indiqué le chemin de l’honneur à suivre », a-t-il déclaré. Un encouragement qui rejoint le message porté par Adama Kadé Touré, déterminée à faire de son expérience une source de motivation pour les jeunes qui souhaitent se lancer dans l’écriture. Lire, travailler et oser franchir le pas À l’occasion de cette dédicace, la jeune auteure a également adressé un message à ses camarades et amis, les invitant à poursuivre leurs objectifs, quels que soient les domaines dans lesquels ils évoluent. « Je voudrais les encourager dans tout ce qu’ils font, que ce soit dans l’art, la technologie et tout autre domaine, à avancer et à faire de leur mieux », a-t-elle lancé, convaincue que la persévérance permet d’aller loin dans la réalisation de ses rêves. Pour Adama Kadé Touré, l’écriture ne doit pas rester une démarche solitaire. Elle doit aussi permettre au lecteur de prendre part à l’aventure, de partager ses propres expériences et, pourquoi pas, de se lancer à son tour. « Mon ouvrage « Afrique, ta jeunesse t’écrit » est un ouvrage miroir. C’est : je te donne, tu me redonnes. Moi, je pars de ce que je peux bien ressentir ou la vision que je peux avoir, mais ce n’est pas moi seulement qui dois parler. Mon lecteur aussi doit s’y mettre et si ça ne suffit pas, c’est l’occasion d’acheter un carnet et un stylo et de s’y mettre à l’écriture », a-t-elle expliqué. Consciente d’être encore au début de son parcours, la jeune écrivaine a conclu avec humilité, tout en laissant entrevoir la suite de son aventure littéraire. « Je sais que je suis encore au début de mon parcours, que j’ai beaucoup à apprendre, beaucoup à découvrir et sûrement beaucoup de livres à écrire » . À travers cette présentation et dédicace, Adama Kadé Touré confirme ainsi son ambition de faire de la littérature un espace de transmission, de dialogue et d’expression pour la jeunesse guinéenne et africaine. items.title: Techiman North inaugurates 58 sanitation guards to boost cleanliness and create jobs
items.description: The Techiman North District Assembly has inaugurated 58 sanitation guards tasked with keeping the district clean and healthy, in a move to tackle poor sanitation and youth unemployment simultaneously. The newly recruited environmental guards were officially outdoored at a brief ceremony held at the Assembly premises in Tuobodom, marking a significant step in the district’s resolve to improve sanitation standards while creating employment opportunities for the teeming unemployed youth. Addressing the gathering, the District Chief Executive (DCE) for Techiman North, Hon. Adom Kwabena Johnson, explained that the initiative serves two critical purposes. “This move will not only help improve the sanitation situation in our district but will also augment the government’s monthly cleanup exercises,” the DCE stated. “We believe that by empowering our youth to take charge of their environment, we are building a healthier and more prosperous district.” The DCE emphasized that the Assembly is committed to ensuring the guards work under safe and dignified conditions. To this end, he announced that the Assembly had procured adequate Personal Protective Equipment (PPEs) to aid their work. The equipment provided to the sanitation guards includes hand gloves, nose masks, reflective jackets, Wellington boots, wheelbarrows, rakes, shovels, and brooms. In a significant boost to waste management efforts, the Assembly also procured two tricycles specifically for the evacuation of refuse after cleanups. “This is a complete package,” the DCE noted. “We are not just giving them jobs; we are giving them the tools they need to do those jobs effectively and safely.” Hon. Johnson also used the occasion to appeal to residents to cooperate with the environmental guards, urging them to see the new recruits as partners in progress rather than intruders. “I urge all residents to cooperate with the environmental guards who are here to help with sanitation services. Let us support them, encourage them, and work together to make Techiman North the cleanest district in the region,” he added. The District Environmental Officer, Mr. Anass Baba Iddrisu, could not hide his excitement about the initiative. He expressed confidence that the new workforce would help sanitize the environment entirely. “This is a dream come true for the environmental department,” Mr. Iddrisu said. “For a long time, we have struggled with inadequate personnel to maintain cleanliness across the district. With these 58 guards on board, I am confident that we will see a remarkable transformation in our sanitation standards.” He added that the environmental guards would be deployed to various communities across the district to ensure that waste is properly managed and the environment is kept clean at all times. For the new recruits, the opportunity represents more than just a job—it is a chance to contribute to their community and secure a livelihood. Speaking on behalf of her colleagues, Ms. Brako Helena expressed gratitude to the Assembly for the opportunity. “We are thankful to the authorities for giving us this chance to serve,” she said. “We pledge to help keep the environment clean. We will not let the Assembly or the people of Techiman North down.” The recruits, who cut across different communities in the district, will undergo orientation on proper waste management, sanitation practices, and environmental health before being deployed to their various stations. The Techiman North initiative is being viewed as a model that other districts could adopt. By combining sanitation improvement with job creation, the Assembly is addressing two critical Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)—Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) and Goal 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth)—at the local level.

items.title: Tunis | Le procès de Moez Haj Mansour fixé au 3 décembre
items.description: Le ministère public près le Tribunal de première instance de Tunis a émis, ce samedi 21 novembre 2026, un mandat de dépôt à l'encontre de Moez Haj Mansour. Il a été déféré en état d'arrestation devant la chambre correctionnelle, qui examinera son dossier lors d'une audience qui a été fixée au 3 décembre prochain. Cette décision fait suite à la mesure de garde à vue, ordonnée il y a deux jours, par le parquet de Tunis auprès des agents de la sous-direction des affaires criminelles de la direction de la police judiciaire d’El Gorjani. On notera que l'affaire est liée à une plainte déposée en mai dernier par le chef du contentieux de l’État, agissant au nom du ministère de l’Intérieur ainsi que de ses cadres et agents, selon le site Babnet, qui précise que Moez Haj Mansour est poursuivi pour « imputation de faits illégaux à un fonctionnaire public en rapport avec ses fonctions sans en établir la véracité» et « traitement de données personnelles sans le consentement de l'intéressé ». La même source ajoute que la plainte du contentieux de l'État porte sur des publications diffusées sur les réseaux sociaux en septembre 2025, à travers lesquelles l'activiste aurait tenu des propos diffamatoires et divulgué l'identité de hauts responsables sécuritaires, exposant ainsi leur vie au danger. Y. N. L’article Tunis | Le procès de Moez Haj Mansour fixé au 3 décembre est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Tinubu cancels Oyo rally fanfare over ‎Bayelsa boat tragedy
items.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA – PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu on Saturday, directed that the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without the usual fanfare in honour of victims of the boat tragedy in Bayelsa State. ‎The President’s decision followed the capsizing of a passenger boat on Friday at Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, leaving several people dead. ‎The victims were reportedly mourners travelling by boat to attend a funeral in the community when the vessel capsized. ‎President Tinubu in a statement by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga expressed sadness over the unfortunate incident and directed that all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation. ‎The statement read: “I am deeply saddened by the tragic incident on Friday in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, where a boat carrying scores of people capsized, resulting in the loss of life. ‎”The deceased were said to be mourners travelling to attend a funeral in the community where the incident happened. ‎”Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation. ‎”I have also directed that our Presidential Campaign Rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, this Saturday, November 21, 2026, be observed without much fanfare in honour of the lives lost and in sympathy with the relatives and families of those involved in the disaster. ‎”On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State. ‎”I particularly mourn with Governor Duoye Diri over this sad incident. I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families.” Vanguard News The post Tinubu cancels Oyo rally fanfare over ‎Bayelsa boat tragedy appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: « Boxer pour l’honneur » : Mamoudou Axcel Keïta dénonce les difficultés d’organisation de la 3e édition à Labé
items.description: Fort d’un parcours remarquable, jalonné de nombreux combats et de trophées remportés sur les rings internationaux, Mamoudou Axcel Keïta a animé, ce samedi 21 novembre 2026, une conférence de presse à la Maison des journalistes, au quartier Minière. À cette occasion, il a exposé les difficultés auxquelles son équipe est confrontée dans le cadre de l’organisation de la troisième édition de « Boxeurs pour l’Honneur », prévue à Labé du 16 au 18 décembre 2026. Au programme de cet événement figurent notamment un sacrifice, des panels sur l’entrepreneuriat féminin, ainsi que des compétitions de sports de combat. Après plusieurs tentatives infructueuses pour obtenir une audience auprès du département en charge des Sports, Mamoudou Axcel Keïta a révélé avoir finalement eu besoin de l’intervention d’un intermédiaire pour être reçu, avec son équipe, par le ministre des Sports, Mamadou Cellou Baldé. Face aux médias, le champion international a expliqué que cette conférence de presse avait notamment pour objectif de solliciter le soutien des personnes de bonne volonté, mais aussi et surtout celui du ministère des Sports et du président de la République, afin de permettre la concrétisation de ce projet au mois de décembre prochain à Labé. L’ambition des initiateurs est de faire de Labé, le temps de quelques jours, la capitale africaine des sports de combat, tout en offrant une vitrine au tourisme, à la culture et au savoir-faire guinéens. Pour Mamoudou Axcel Keïta, le choix de Labé pour accueillir cette troisième édition ne relève nullement du hasard. « On a choisi d'abord Labé pour son hospitalité, sa spiritualité. C'est une ville qui me tient au cœur, ville d’origine de ma grand-mère maternelle, où j'ai passé une partie de mon enfance en venant en vacances à Labé et tout. Et après beaucoup d'années d'absence, il y a juste une semaine, j'étais à Labé pour venir soumettre mon projet aux autorités, aux organisations et aux structures et on m'avait accueilli, j’étais tellement content que j'ai su à partir de ce moment même que m'étais pas trompé du choix de Labé. L'accueil était de taille ». Revenant sur la portée de cette initiative, ce boxeur international, considéré comme l’une des grandes figures des sports de combat en Guinée, a exprimé son souhait de voir le projet s’inscrire dans la durée. « Maintenant, ce projet de Boxeurs pour Honneur, c'est un truc que je vais continuer à faire même après ma mort, une équipe plus jeunes que moi, la structure donc pourrait continuer, j'espère. On peut pas faire des événements de telle envergure sans l'appui d'un gouvernement, ce n’est pas possible. Même si je veux, je ne pourrais pas. On a passé voir le ministère de tutelle. Déjà ça a pris beaucoup de temps, on a fait beaucoup de rendez-vous, on a essayé beaucoup de fois. Il a fallu l'intervention d'un médiateur pour que je sois reçu par le monsieur le ministre de Sports. Le pourquoi, je ne sais pas ». Évoquant les engagements pris lors de sa rencontre avec le ministre des Sports, ce champion à plusieurs reprises de boxe thaïlandaise est également revenu sur les assurances qui lui auraient été données à cette occasion. « Et quand j'ai été reçu avec mon équipe, il y a eu des promesses qui se sont tenues là-bas. Pour l'accompagnement de ce projet à Labé. Le ministre même avait publié sur sa page et aux pages du ministère de Sports en disant que le mois de décembre c'était maintenant. Et donc, en vrai dit, on était sortis du Ministère soulagés et très contents. On a commencé à partir de ce moment de fournir l'effort au niveau de l'organisation pour avoir tout prêt avant cet moment ». Le champion international de boxe thaïlandaise et expert en arts martiaux a toutefois déploré l'absence de suivi depuis cette rencontre, qui remonterait au 13 juin dernier. Il affirme avoir multiplié les démarches pour obtenir une nouvelle audience auprès du ministre, sans succès jusqu'à présent. « Mais depuis qu'on avait quitté, c'était le 13 juin au Ministère de Sports, depuis là on a plus été accueilli là-bas. Le pourquoi, on ne sait pas. On a tenté, on a fait beaucoup de tentatives, ils ont essuyé. Comme la première fois c'était grâce à un médiateur pour que je sois reçu par le monsieur le ministre, et cette fois-ci, je suis encore en train de chercher ce médiateur pour pouvoir rencontrer le ministre », a-t-il déploré. Véritable ambassadeur du sport guinéen sur la scène internationale, Mamoudou Axcel Keïta a également fait part de ses inquiétudes quant aux répercussions que cette situation pourrait avoir sur sa crédibilité, mais aussi sur celle de la Guinée. « Pour être précis, j'ai octroyé le drapeau guinéen dans 47 pays. Si ma crédibilité doit être en jeu quelque part, je pense que ça devrait pas être la Guinée. Pourquoi ? Parce que je me suis battu pour pour ce pays. Et donc, il y a ma crédibilité qui est en jeu, il y a une soixantaine de boxeurs qui comptent combattre le mois de décembre là à Labé. Mon téléphone n'arrête pas de sonner. Jusqu'à présent après notre accueil au Ministère de Sports, en fait, le projet n'a pas été matérialisé ». Pour Mamoudou Axcel Keïta, le sport constitue un puissant levier de transformation sociale. C’est dans cette perspective qu’il a choisi de mettre son expérience, son expertise et sa notoriété au service de son pays. « Son ambition est de contribuer à la création d’opportunités pour la jeunesse, de promouvoir les valeurs de discipline, de respect, de paix et d’excellence, tout en participant au rayonnement international de la Guinée et de l’Afrique. C’est dans cette dynamique qu’est né le Gala International Boxeurs pour l’Honneur », un rendez-vous qui ambitionne de dépasser le simple cadre d’une compétition de boxe. Véritable plateforme de promotion du sport, de la culture, du tourisme, de l’entrepreneuriat et de la coopération internationale, cette initiative entend positionner la Guinée comme une destination incontournable des sports de combat sur le continent africain», rappelle Mohamed Negué Kouyaté, secrétaire général de la structure. De son côté, le directeur général de Fanca Events, Fana Condé, a insisté sur la nécessité d’un accompagnement du ministère de tutelle, tout en revenant sur les engagements pris par le ministre des Sports lors de sa cérémonie de passation de service. « Aujourd'hui, on peut pas évoluer sans le Ministère de tutelle. Et le Ministère de tutelle, quand on parle de Ministère de tutelle, on s'adresse directement au ministre. Si le président de la République a porté confiance au ministre pour pouvoir gérer le sport. Le ministre on compte sur lui pour pouvoir aussi respecter ses engagements. Il y a une seule chose qui nous a marqué à la cérémonie de passation de service du ministre, il avait réitéré en disant que « il ne sera jamais le ministre du football ». Et ça, c'est une déclaration donc qui a marqué tout le monde. Il a dit qu’il ne va pas se consacrer juste pour le football, il va aider aussi les autres sports. C'est un engagement solennel et qui mérite aujourd'hui d'être vraiment respecté et tout le monde doit soutenir le ministre dans ce sens. Et on sait que tout le sport se vaut, mais le football on sait que c'est le sport roi. Mais c'est le ministre lui-même qui avait pris l'engagement solennel de le dire. Donc, on compte sur lui aujourd'hui ». Il convient de rappeler que ce boxeur de nationalité guinéo-néerlandaise a, au fil de sa carrière, disputé de nombreux combats professionnels sur les rings internationaux, affrontant des adversaires de très haut niveau. Au terme de 26 années de carrière, son bilan sportif fait état de 110 combats disputés dans 47 pays, dont la Guinée, avec 74 victoires, parmi lesquelles 44 obtenues par KO, 32 défaites et 5 matchs nuls. Mamoudou Yaya Barry L’article « Boxer pour l’honneur » : Mamoudou Axcel Keïta dénonce les difficultés d’organisation de la 3e édition à Labé est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: L’Ukraine, une «vache à lait» pour la CIA, selon l’ancien chef de cabinet de Colin Powell
items.description: La CIA a pratiquement cesse de produire du renseignement strategique et mene desormais des « operations clandestines en fonction de ce qui lui rapporte le plus ». C'est ce qu'a declare le colonel a la retraite et ancien chef de cabinet du secretaire d'etat Colin Powell de 2002 a 2005, Lawrence Wilkerson, a propos des activites de l'agence de renseignement americaine, le 18 novembre dans le podcast « Judging Freedom » du juge Andrew Napolitano, a la veille du sommet trilateral entre Trump, Xi Jinping et Vladimir Poutine en Chine. Deux hypotheses aussi graves l'une que l'autre Durant l'emission, Andrew Napolitano a evoque la frappe ukrainienne contre le pont de Crimee, reliant la peninsule a la Russie metropolitaine, indiquant qu'une operation du genre « n'aurait pas pu etre menee sans la CIA americaine ». Dans ce contexte, il a pose la question suivante : comment le president pouvait « fraterniser avec le president russe alors que la CIA, qui travaille theoriquement pour lui, s'en prend a des infrastructures et des monuments russes de premier plan ». La reponse de Lawrence Wilkerson s'est articulee en deux hypotheses aussi graves l'une que l'autre. Dans une premiere hypothese, l'ancien chef de cabinet suppose que Donald Trump « n'etait au courant de rien », une possibilite qu'il declare « pouvoir croire sans difficulte, etant donne a quel point la CIA, le SIS et [le Mossad] agissent de maniere incontrolee ces derniers temps ». Pour la seconde hypothese, Lawrence Wilkerson declare qu'« il ne s'agit que d'une manœuvre de plus, du genre de celles auxquelles se livrent certains individus – surtout ceux qui, comme Trump, s'imaginent experts en la matiere alors qu'ils ne le sont guere ». Quelle que soit l'hypothese adoptee, dans les deux cas, la CIA pourrait « absolument », selon Lawrence Wilkerson, attaquer une infrastructure majeure d'un gouvernement etranger sans l'autorisation du president. Operations clandestines : l'essentiel du « business » de la CIA Pour le colonel a la retraite, les operations clandestines constituent l'essentiel du « business » de la CIA. Il affirme que « ce qu'ils font, ce sont des operations clandestines, en fonction de ce qui leur rapporte le plus. Il s'agit, en regle generale, de conflits ou de situations proches du conflit ». Dans ce contexte, il assure que l'Ukraine « est une veritable aubaine pour eux [la CIA] ». Allant encore plus loin, Lawrence Wilkerson declare que l'Ukraine est « une veritable vache a lait. Et, avec la guerre actuelle, c'est devenu une mine d'or extraordinaire », ajoute-t-il. Avant d'assener : « Ils [la CIA] sont capables de generer leurs propres fonds a un rythme encore plus soutenu — depassant meme les 15 milliards de dollars qu'ils recoivent actuellement du gouvernement ; une realite de laquelle, je le soupconne, Trump n'a pas la moindre idee. » Une proposition inconcevable pour le Kremlin a propos de l'Ukraine et de l'OTAN, Andrew Napolitano souleve la question de la proposition posee sur la table lors des discussions a Abou Dhabi, suggerant d'accepter la cession officielle du Donbass a la Russie. En contrepartie, l'Ukraine pourrait alors integrer l'OTAN. Pour Lawrence Wilkerson, l'idee d'un tel accord est qualifiee d'inconcevable pour le Kremlin. Il precise que celui qui l'a formulee « est soit d'une stupidite abyssale, soit ne comprend absolument pas quelle est la veritable preoccupation de Poutine ». La Russie place l'elargissement de l'OTAN vers l'est au cœur de ses preoccupations, s'opposant categoriquement a toute adhesion de l'Ukraine a l'Alliance atlantique, consideree comme incompatible avec ses exigences de securite. Cette position comptait parmi les raisons majeures invoquees par Moscou pour expliquer son operation militaire speciale dans le Donbass. Lors de sa participation a l'APEC, le president russe a rappele que l'Ukraine avait initialement inscrit le principe de neutralite dans sa declaration d'independance, avant de s'orienter vers l'OTAN. Pour Vladimir Poutine, l'Occident a ignore pendant bien longtemps les preoccupations securitaires de la Russie, reiterant le refus d'une adhesion de Kiev a l'OTAN, soulignant la necessite d'une prise en compte des interets de securite de la Russie comme condition sine qua non a tout reglement durable du conflit.

items.title: Resurge en Italia el misterio de las masacres de la Mafia de 1992 con el suicidio de un exjefe de policía
items.description: Uno de los asuntos más oscuros de la historia reciente de Italia, las masacres de la Mafia siciliana de 1992, que acabaron con la vida de los jueces Giovanni Falcone y Paolo Borsellino , resurge del pasado y demuestra que queda aún mucho por saber y resolver: Gianni de Gennaro, alias el Tiburón , el superpolicía que era la mano derecha de Falcone, gran héroe de la lucha contra la Mafia en los años ochenta y noventa, se ha suicidado en su casa de campo en Montiano, Toscana, según ha informado la prensa italiana. Su cuerpo ha sido hallado en la mañana de este sábado y la policía analiza una pistola hallada junto a él. Por la tarde, los medios han indicado que se han encontrado notas de despedida a sus familiares y documentos judiciales. Es una noticia que supone un terremoto en Italia y remueve uno de los traumas más profundos de la conciencia colectiva del país, por las sospechas no aclaradas de complicidad de las altas esferas de la política y del Estado en aquellos crímenes. items.title: Asiedu Nketiah urges Africa to turn reparations declarations into practical action
items.description: By Isaac Yeboah National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, has called on African governments and political leaders to move beyond declarations on reparative justice and pursue practical measures capable of securing redress for historical injustices. He says Africa has made significant progress in building the institutional framework for reparations but must now give the process greater political support and ensure that commitments translate into enforceable remedies. Addressing the Movement for Freedom of Nations Assembly in Moscow on November 16, 2026, Mr Asiedu Nketiah said the African Union had established mechanisms to develop a common position on reparations and was working with Caribbean institutions to coordinate legal analysis and diplomacy. He cited the Accra Reparations Conference of 2023, the African Union’s designation of 2025 as the Year of Justice for Africans and People of African Descent Through Reparations, and the Decade of Justice and Reparations for 2026 to 2035 as important milestones. He also acknowledged the work of the African Union Committee of Experts on Reparations and its Reference Group of Legal Experts in examining the legal, economic, cultural and institutional dimensions of the issue. Mr Asiedu Nketiah said cooperation between the African Union and the Caribbean Community (CARICOM) was important in building a coordinated campaign, while recognising that the historical experiences and remedies sought by different communities might not be identical. He commended President John Dramani Mahama, Ghana’s leadership in the reparations campaign and his role as the African Union Champion on Reparations. He also referenced United Nations General Assembly Resolution 80/250, adopted on March 25, 2026, saying the 123 votes in favour represented important international recognition of the gravity of the trafficking and enslavement of Africans. However, he cautioned that the Movement for Freedom of Nations should complement rather than duplicate the work of established African Union and Caribbean institutions. He proposed that the Movement could support the process by facilitating access to historical archives, encouraging dialogue with museums and public authorities, and using its relationships with governments and parliaments to advance the work of existing expert bodies. Mr Asiedu Nketiah said political declarations alone would not secure justice without the legislative, administrative and diplomatic action needed to implement them. “If legislation prevents the return of cultural property, a parliament must examine it. If an agreement is reached, a government must define and honour its obligations,” he said. He further insisted that communities affected by historical injustices must have a say in the design of reparative agreements and be able to hold those responsible accountable. The NDC Chairman also cautioned against presenting ordinary development projects as reparations without demonstrating their connection to the historical wrongs being addressed. He said apologies, restitution, compensation, access to archives, educational measures and institutional reforms could each address different forms of injustice and should be assessed according to the harm they seek to remedy. Mr Asiedu Nketiah stressed that the pursuit of reparations should not absolve contemporary African governments of their responsibility to govern effectively, create opportunities and account for public resources. Equally, he said, failures by present governments should not invalidate legitimate claims arising from historical injustices. “We have reached a point at which Africa need not merely repeat the case it has made for decades,” he said, urging political leaders to give the existing reparations process practical assistance and ensure that recognition is followed by lasting remedies.

items.title: Ashantis deserve more than loans of their stolen royal regalia – Asiedu Nketiah
items.description: By Isaac Yeboah The National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, says the Asante people deserve more than temporary access to their royal heritage, insisting that the return of looted regalia on loan from British museums cannot be equated with full restitution. He says the distinction between a loan and a transfer of ownership is important in assessing whether communities whose cultural treasures were taken during colonial conquest have received meaningful redress. Speaking at the Movement for Freedom of Nations Assembly in Moscow on November 16, 2026, Mr Asiedu Nketiah cited the return of Asante royal regalia for public display at the Manhyia Palace Museum in Kumasi as an example of the complexities surrounding cultural restitution. He acknowledged the negotiations that facilitated the arrangements but stressed that some of the objects had been fully restituted while others were only on loan from British museums. “We appreciate the negotiations that made those arrangements possible, but a loan is not the same as a transfer of ownership,” he said. The NDC Chairman argued that the rights restored and the obligations accepted must be central to any assessment of remedies for historical injustices. His remarks bring renewed attention to the question of ownership of Asante royal artefacts taken during British colonial military campaigns and subsequently held in foreign museums and collections. For the Asante people, he suggested, the return of such objects should not be judged merely by whether they can be displayed in Ghana, but also by whether ownership has been restored to the community from which they were taken. Mr Asiedu Nketiah said claims arising from cultural seizure, enslavement, forced labour and dispossession required different forms of redress. While the provenance and ownership of identifiable objects could be investigated, he said broader claims arising from the transatlantic slave trade raised more complex questions of responsibility, applicable law and the people entitled to benefit from reparations. He maintained that the complexity of the issues should not be used as a reason to delay action. “A credible claim must rest on evidence, and a credible response must be capable of implementation,” he said. The NDC Chairman also called for communities affected by historical injustices to have a voice in the design of reparative agreements and mechanisms to hold responsible parties accountable. He cautioned that development projects should not automatically be presented as reparations simply because they are given that description. “The connection between the wrong and the proposed remedy must be demonstrated, and the outcome must be open to scrutiny by those asked to accept it,” he said. Mr Asiedu Nketiah was addressing an assembly of political leaders and delegates on reparative justice and the African Union. He urged the Movement for Freedom of Nations to support existing African Union and Caribbean reparations mechanisms rather than establish parallel institutions. His comments come as the African Union advances its Decade of Justice and Reparations for 2026 to 2035, following its designation of 2025 as the Year of Justice for Africans and People of African Descent Through Reparations.

items.title: Chelsea humbled as Leeds run riot
items.description: Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds on Saturday as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches. Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke’s men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to west London. Just 24 hours after NFL legend Tom Brady was linked with buying a minority stake in Chelsea, the seven-time Super Bowl winner might be thinking twice about his mooted investment. Brady is believed to be friendly with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali, who will have a big decision to make on Alonso’s future if results do not improve soon. Chelsea are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso, who was hyped as the stabilising force the club needed after a turbulent period. Alonso has been hampered by the absence of injured Brazilian striker Joao Pedro in recent weeks and once again Chelsea struggled without their attacking talisman. Making his full debut in Alonso’s latest bid to find a stand-in for Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute. Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home. Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front. Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage-time to leave Chelsea in turmoil. Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool. While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager. Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. items.title: Ukraine : Mélenchon met Paris en garde contre une confrontation avec la Russie
items.description: « Si la puissance qui est en guerre vous dit : attention, vous etes en train de devenir un cobelligerant, on discute. » Jean-Luc Melenchon estime que Paris ferait bien de prendre cet avertissement au serieux. Le 20 novembre, devant les etudiants de Sciences Po, le candidat a la presidentielle de La France insoumise (LFI) a rappele que le soutien a Kiev ne devait pas entraîner la France dans un affrontement avec la Russie. Son exemple est brutal : une frappe contre la centrale nucleaire de Nogent-sur-Seine. Jean-Luc Melenchon imagine les consequences d'un tel scenario pour la France, dont il compare la taille a celle de la Russie, etendue sur onze fuseaux horaires. a ses yeux, une mise en garde de Moscou appelle une discussion, pas une surenchere. Moscou avertit, Paris replique Le 17 novembre, des informations sur la presence de militaires francais en Ukraine , notamment pour la formation et la maintenance, ont relance la polemique. Sergueï Lavrov, le ministre russe des Affaires etrangeres, considere que cette presence impliquerait directement Paris dans le conflit. Alice Rufo, ministre deleguee aux Armees, conteste cette lecture en faisant valoir qu'il ne s'agit pas de missions de combat. Le leader de La France insoumise a relaye l'avertissement de Moscou en ecrivant : « Alerte. Nous ne devons en aucun cas devenir cobelligerant en Ukraine. » Il insistait sur le danger d'une confrontation avec une puissance nucleaire. Le 18 novembre, au Senat, Jean-Noel Barrot, ministre francais des Affaires etrangeres, a pourtant accuse Jean-Luc Melenchon d'avoir « tout simplement repercute la propagande de M. Lavrov ». L'echange a deplace le debat du risque militaire vers l'accusation de proximite avec Moscou. Une mise en garde qui ne date pas d'hier Ce discours n'est pas ne de la seule conference de Sciences Po. Des le 7 novembre, au Bourget, l'ancien socialiste denoncait les responsables favorables a l'escalade, evoquant un affrontement contre un etat dote de l'arme nucleaire. Il avertissait alors : « On ne peut pas jouer avec ces questions-la. » Dans le meme discours, il reprochait aux dirigeants europeens d'avoir laisse s'ouvrir des negociations sans eux et plaidait pour des garanties de securite concernant aussi la Russie. Il defendait egalement le droit des habitants du Donbass a etre entendus en cas de modification des frontieres, ce qui lui avait deja valu des accusations de proximite avec le Kremlin. a Sciences Po, il a reaffirme le droit des habitants du Donbass a etre entendus, tout en declarant les frontieres ukrainiennes non negociables. Cette position prend une autre dimension a l'approche de la presidentielle de 2027. Dans une enquete de Politico relayee le 20 novembre , plusieurs diplomates europeens et ukrainiens s'inquietent d'un eventuel changement de cap a Paris. Sur huit responsables interroges, environ la moitie redoutent qu'une victoire de Jean-Luc Melenchon ou de Marine Le Pen n'affaiblisse le consensus europeen sur le soutien a Kiev. La question depasse les seules livraisons d'armes. La France copreside la « Coalition des volontaires » et joue un role dans les discussions sur les garanties de securite de l'Ukraine. Elle dispose aussi d'un droit de veto sur le renouvellement des sanctions europeennes contre Moscou, qui exige l'unanimite des etats membres. Un changement de position de Paris pourrait donc compliquer leur prolongation. Cette perspective preoccupe notamment les diplomates attaches a la politique actuelle de l'Union europeenne. Berlin cherche deja a inscrire durablement le financement de Kiev dans le prochain budget europeen, afin de limiter les risques de blocage apres les elections francaises. Les avertissements de Jean-Luc Melenchon sur la cobelligerance s'inscrivent ainsi dans un debat qui depasse sa polemique avec Jean-Noel Barrot. a quelques mois du depart d'Emmanuel Macron, la possibilite d'une politique francaise privilegiant davantage le dialogue avec Moscou devient elle-meme un enjeu de la presidentielle.

items.title: English village votes to ‘leave UK’ over migrant camp plan
items.description: A small English village on Saturday voted to leave the UK in a symbolic poll protesting government plans to house hundreds of asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base. The vote in Barnham follows a similar protest referendum in the village of Piddington in September, also over government plans to move asylum seekers from hotels into former military accommodation. Between 400 to 500 people were eligible to vote in the ballot which carried no legal weight, with 257 voting for independence, 16 against, and one spoilt ballot. “There’s an issue with the sheer volume of people expected to be accommodated,” the chairwoman of the Barnham residents’ association, Helen Beck, told AFP earlier. “Barnham is a small village. There will be nothing for the (lodged) people to do, nowhere to go.” Under plans by Britain’s government, the base near the village in rural eastern England will be used to accommodate 931 migrants. The village has a population of 584. Residents were asked whether they supported seeking a “crown dependency status” similar to that of Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man. Parish council chair John Bauer said this would allow the village to “retain loyalty to the crown” while removing itself from Home Office jurisdiction. – Safety concern – Residents in both Barnham and Piddington say they are also worried about locals’ safety, particularly that of women. “We’ve been told they (the asylum seekers) are all males. We don’t know where they are from, their background,” Beck said. “People are anxious about walking alone, walking their dog in darkness if an additional 900 men arrive in the area,” she said. In the Piddington vote in September, 285 out of 312 votes were cast in favour of “pursuing self-determination”. The government plans to house around 1,250 asylum seekers on a former defence ministry site close to Piddington village, all single men between 18 and 65. Britain’s centre-left government, in power since July 2024, has vowed to end the use of hotels as migrant accommodation following a public outcry. It plans to move all those currently in hotels — a policy inherited from the last Conservative government — to former military bases by 2029. But Beck said that there were questions about whether military-style accommodation was suitable for people “fleeing a conflict or persecution”, adding that it was also “significantly more expensive than hotels”.
