items.title: L’Algérie débloque 500 millions de dollars pour les chemins de fer
items.description: L’Algérie mise sur le chemin de fer pour accélérer le développement de vastes régions du sud du pays et l’exploitation de ses ressources minières. Elle vient de débloquer une enveloppe de 68,26 milliards de dinars, soit environ 500 millions de dollars au taux de change actuel. « Il est ouvert, sur 2026, un montant de soixante-huit milliards deux cent soixante millions de dinars (68.260.000.000 DA) en autorisations d'engagement, applicable au programme « Infrastructures ferroviaires et transports guidés », au sous-programme « Développement des infrastructures ferroviaires » et au titre 3 « Dépenses d'investissement » du portefeuille de programmes du ministère des travaux publics et des infrastructures de base », a indiqué un décret présidentiel publié au Journal officiel. Le décret ne précise pas pour quel projet cet argent a été débloqué. Algérie : voici les trois plus grands projets ferroviaires stratégiques Des projets colossaux à coup de milliards de dollars ont été lancés ces dernières années pour construire trois nouvelles lignes ferroviaires stratégiques. La première pour relier le gisement de minerai de fer de Gara Djebilet à Béchar sur 950 km qui a été inaugurée le 1er février dernier par le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune. La deuxième voie ferrée a été lancée pour raccorder le gisement de phosphate de Blad el Hadba dans la wilaya de Tébessa au port d’Annaba sur 425 km. Son rôle est double : transporter le phosphate jusqu’à ce grand port et les voyageurs entre la grande ville de l’est algérien et l’extrême est du pays. Ce chantier est en cours et la ligne devrait être livrée durant le premier trimestre 2027. Le troisième grand chantier ferroviaire lancé par l’Algérie est la construction d’une voie ferrée entre Alger et Tamanrasset dans l’extrême sud du pays sur plus de 2000 km dont 308 km sont déjà achevés. Montant total pour réaliser ce qui reste : 14,6 milliards de dollars. Le président Tebboune a donné des instructions pour que le train siffle à Tamanrasset en 2028. L’article L'Algérie débloque 500 millions de dollars pour les chemins de fer est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: CAF : la commission des arbitres dissoute sous la supervision de la FIFA
items.description: La Confédération africaine de football (CAF) s'apprête à ouvrir un nouveau chapitre dans la gestion de l'arbitrage sur le continent. La Commission des arbitres, dirigée par le Congolais Olivier Safari Kabene, serait sur le point d'être dissoute puis reconstituée avec l'implication de la Fédération internationale de football (FIFA). Cette réorganisation intervient dans un climat de défiance grandissante à l'égard de l'arbitrage africain. Selon plusieurs informations relayées ce samedi, la décision aurait été prise à Abuja, au Nigeria, à la suite de nombreuses récriminations formulées par des fédérations nationales. Les dysfonctionnements dénoncés concerneraient notamment la gestion des arbitres, leur désignation et le fonctionnement de l'organe chargé de superviser les officiels lors des compétitions continentales. L'annonce officielle de cette réforme reste toutefois attendue. La finale Sénégal-Maroc toujours dans les mémoires La dernière Coupe d'Afrique des nations (CAN) a largement contribué à fragiliser la crédibilité de la structure dirigée par Safari Kabene. La finale entre le Sénégal et le Maroc, disputée le 18 janvier 2026 à Rabat, avait été marquée par de fortes tensions, notamment après la décision de l'arbitre congolais Jean-Jacques Ndala d'accorder un penalty au Maroc et l'interruption momentanée de la rencontre. La polémique avait pris une autre dimension après les déclarations d'Olivier Safari Kabene sur son intervention dans la gestion disciplinaire de certains joueurs sénégalais. Ces révélations avaient soulevé des interrogations sur les limites de l'intervention de la commission dans le travail des arbitres et sur l'indépendance de ces derniers. Plus récemment, la rencontre entre la Libye et la Tunisie (1-1), disputée le 17 novembre dans le cadre des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027, a ravivé les critiques. Les Tunisiens avaient vivement contesté un penalty accordé aux Libyens dans le temps additionnel de la première période. La réaction de plusieurs responsables de la Fédération tunisienne aurait contribué à accélérer la remise en question de la commission. La FIFA dans le dispositif de réforme La restructuration envisagée devrait accorder une place plus importante à la FIFA dans la supervision de l'arbitrage africain. L'objectif serait de revoir les mécanismes de désignation et de contrôle des arbitres, tout en renforçant la transparence et les compétences techniques de la nouvelle équipe. Cette évolution s'inscrirait dans le prolongement des engagements pris par la CAF en mars 2026, lorsque Patrice Motsepe avait annoncé des réformes des statuts et règlements pour restaurer la confiance envers les arbitres, les opérateurs de l'assistance vidéo (VAR) et les instances juridictionnelles. Au-delà du changement de responsables, le véritable défi sera de garantir l'indépendance des arbitres, de professionnaliser leur encadrement et de mettre fin aux soupçons d'influence. Car la crédibilité des compétitions africaines dépend aussi de la confiance accordée à ceux qui en garantissent l'équité. C.G. DIOP

items.title: South Africa reopens the business of winning Ghanaian travellers and corporate clients
items.description: South Africa is stepping up efforts to rebuild confidence among Ghanaian travellers, business operators and corporate clients, as tourism stakeholders seek to turn recent travel sentiment challenges into renewed commercial opportunities. A networking engagement at South Africa House in Cantonments brought together the South African High Commission, South African Tourism and South African Airways (SAA) in a coordinated effort to reconnect with Ghana’s travel trade, corporate community and media, while reaffirming South Africa’s readiness to welcome visitors from Ghana. The event, themed South Africa Awaits – Come Find Your Joy , comes at a time when immigration-related tensions and reports of xenophobic incidents have affected perceptions of travel to South Africa. While the organisers sought to reassure prospective travellers, the engagement was also about rebuilding commercial relationships, stimulating travel demand and opening new avenues of cooperation between businesses in the two countries. For South Africa, Ghana represents more than a leisure travel market. The country’s long-standing commercial relationship with South Africa, the presence of South African businesses operating locally and the potential for companies to use travel as a tool for employee reward, business development and networking provide a wider economic proposition. Political Counsellor at the South African High Commission, Phoka Motsilili, said the networking session was intended to bring South African tourism institutions closer to Ghanaian operators and encourage collaboration in promoting the destination. He stressed that tourism was an important economic sector because of its capacity to create employment, arguing that the promotional effort predated the recent tensions. Among the practical outcomes being pursued is the development of group travel packages through South African Airways for Ghanaians visiting South Africa. Motsilili also reaffirmed that Ghanaian visitors, including tourists and students, were welcome in South Africa, with assurances that their safety remained a priority. The business case for travel was further strengthened by Bongiwe Nzeku, Head of Business Development and Support Services at the South Africa National Convention Bureau, who outlined opportunities for Ghanaian companies interested in meetings, incentive travel and corporate programmes in South Africa. Through the Bureau’s bid support programme, companies bringing groups of at least 50 delegates to South Africa for meetings or incentive trips can access financial support towards their costs. The programme provides an opportunity for Ghanaian organisations to consider South Africa not only for leisure travel, but also for conferences, reward programmes, employee engagement and corporate gatherings. Nzeku encouraged companies to rethink how they reward high-performing employees, presenting incentive travel as an opportunity to combine recognition with destination experiences. Options range from dining experiences in the Kruger National Park to meals overlooking Table Mountain, illustrating the breadth of experiences available to corporate groups. She also pointed to the potential of companies with established links to both markets, citing MTN’s 30-year presence in Ghana as an example of the type of corporate relationship South Africa would like to engage. South African Airways is also positioning itself to support the corporate travel market through discounted fares for businesses, alongside its group travel offering. The airline’s Country Manager, Gloria Wilkinson-Mensah, said the recent coverage of tensions had contributed to perceptions that South Africa was unsafe and visitors were unwelcome, with the airline recording a decline in passenger loads. However, SAA maintained its operations throughout the period and continues to offer the only direct Accra-Johannesburg service, connecting travellers onwards to Cape Town, Durban and Port Elizabeth. That connectivity remains important to businesses seeking efficient access to South Africa’s commercial centres, particularly for meetings, partnerships, investment discussions and regional travel. The Ghana South Africa Business Chamber is also urging companies in both markets to look beyond the current climate and explore opportunities to expand their operations. Its CEO, Tony Sekyere, encouraged Ghanaian businesses to consider South Africa while inviting South African companies to pursue opportunities in Ghana. South African Tourism’s Regional Head for West Africa, Thekiso Rakolojane, said Ghana remained a strategic market, supported by deep historical ties and the organisation’s presence in the country since 2013. He acknowledged the decline in arrivals during periods of restricted travel but said demand was improving, with Ghanaians returning for holidays and milestone celebrations. The challenge for South Africa is now to translate renewed engagement into measurable commercial outcomes. Travel packages, corporate incentives, convention support, airline connectivity and business chamber relationships provide the framework. Whether these initiatives lead to increased bookings, corporate trips and new business relationships will determine how successfully South Africa turns its confidence-building campaign into a renewed commercial relationship with Ghana.

items.title: Protect local rice farmers – Dr Bawumia tells government
items.description: The former Vice President and flagbearer of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has called for a decisive shift in national policy to protect local rice producers from rising production costs at home and the falling prices of imported rice. He stated that the biggest challenge facing the sector was imports, which he indicated were too high. Dr Bawumia made these remarks when he interacted with farmers at Asutuare in the Eastern Region last Friday, November 13, 2026, noting that the price of imported rice was lower than that of local production. Citing the Japanese situation to buttress his point, Dr Bawumia said rice in Japan is treated as a matter of national security, and Ghana needed to adopt a similar approach to protect its farmers. “Rice prices in Japan are almost 50 per cent higher than the world price. We import over 50 per cent of rice. In Japan, it is less than 10 per cent,” he stated, adding that the comparison exposed Ghana’s attitude problem towards agriculture. While Japan deliberately protects its farmers, the NPP Flagbearer and former Vice-President said Ghana has left its rice sector exposed to imports that undercut local farmers. He called for an attitudinal change towards agriculture and rice farmers, stressing that “We need to protect our rice farmers in Ghana.” “The imports are too high. The price of the imports is lower than the price of the local production,” he said. A major driver of this disparity, he explained, was the exchange rate. He noted that the cedi’s appreciation had reduced import costs by about 40 per cent in the last two years. “The exchange rate has fallen by 40%. The import cost has come down by 40 per cent. You are hurting the farmers,” he added, noting that at the same time, the cost of production for local farmers had gone up. The result, Dr Bawumia said, is a paradox in which farmers are producing more and more rice but cannot sell it. He noted that the market was flooded with cheaper imports, creating excess capacity and leaving farmers with unsold stock. “You are producing more and more rice. That is why you have excess capacity. The whole Ghana rice farmers, because imports are performing, because the price of those imported bags of rice are performing,” he said. To reverse the trend, the NPP Flagbearer called for a strong strategy and policy framework to protect rice farmers and agriculture as a whole. First, he said, the government must lead by buying local. “As a nation, as a government, we need to buy more local rice for our schools and our prisons. Everywhere, we need to buy more local rice. We need to empower buffer stock to buy more local rice because if you do not, you will create unemployment. It is very, very important,” he pointed out. Furthermore, Dr Bawumia said, “Ghana must deliberately reduce rice imports because we believe that Ghana can be self-sufficient in rice production.” He noted that the country has both the potential and the land to produce enough rice. Central to that self-sufficiency drive, he said, was the availability of water. He, therefore, called for the urgent completion of Phase Two of the Pwalugu Irrigation Project, which has stalled for the last two years. “We should finish the Phase Two of the Pwalugu Irrigation Project so that you can have water to do the production. The last two years, there has been no work,” he said. “And also, some of the various lots, no production for the last two years. Farmers are at home. We need to finish the Phase two.” Dr Bawumia also called for the return of the fertilizer subsidy for farmers to help bring down production costs. Underpinning all these proposals, he said, was a single principle: the nation is vulnerable if it cannot feed itself. He stated that his government would treat agriculture as a matter of national security, adding that when it comes to food, the country should depend on itself. Sharing their concerns, the rice farmers said they were suffering because they had produced rice for two years but could not sell it. “We produce rice and it is our expectation that we are able to sell so that we can make money and look after our children, but unfortunately last year and this year we could not sell the rice,” said a farmer and Secretary of the Northern Low Level Branch of the Water Users Association, Alex Tawiah Amano. He acknowledged that the problem was nationwide but noted that through their network of irrigation schemes, farmers reported the same situation at Asutsuare, Akuse, Kpong and elsewhere. He said buyers were not forthcoming, noting that rice must move in tonnages to empty warehouses. Another rice farmer with over three decades of experience and leader of the Shai-Osudoku Rice Farmers, Sika Bright, who said he represented over 3,500 farmers, noted that thousands of tonnes were packed in mills, with weevils destroying them. “For me alone, it is over 100 tonnes. Farmers have to take loans from banks to do this farm, and at the end of the day, the rice will be there and it will spoil,” he said. A branch chairman with 192 farmers said his 192 hectares have not been cropped since rehabilitation began, and contractors had left the site. He appealed to the government to intervene to create a market for local rice.

items.title: Una productora teatral denuncia al Ayuntamiento de Pinto (PP) por cancelar “por motivos ideológicos” una obra inspirada en Lorca y otros cuatro montajes
items.description: En 2027 se celebra el centenario de la llamada Generación del 27 y “el teatro de Pinto lo celebra cancelando a Lorca”, denuncia la compañía El Aedo Teatro, productora de la obra Poeta perdido en Nueva York , inspirada en el poemario de Lorca, ganadora del premio Max a la mejor producción privada en 2026. La representación de esta obra en el Teatro Municipal Francisco Rabal del municipio madrileño, gobernado por el PP, estaba apalabrada para el mes de abril y no ha sido la única borrada del programa por “motivos ideológicos”, según expone el comunicado de la compañía. El hijo de la cómica , de José Sacristán; Libres , de Teatro del Barrio; El verdugo , de El espejo negro; y La Reina Brava , de Las Niñas de Cádiz son las otras cuatro obras afectadas. Han quedado fuera de la programación para el primer semestre del próximo año en Pinto, según les ha comunicado Daniel Martínez Ramírez, técnico de Juventud, Infancia y Artes Escénicas del ayuntamiento del municipio madrileño encargado de la programación, tras reunirse con la concejala de artes y educación, Verónica Castellano Santiago. items.title: DR Congo: Evaluation conjointe des besoins en matière d’Education et Protection RDC-2026
items.description: Country: Democratic Republic of the Congo Sources: Education Cluster, Save the Children, UN Children's Fund Please refer to the attached file. Le rapport de l’évaluation conjointe des besoins d’Education et de Protection menée en collaboration avec le secteur de la Protection met en évidence les résultats suivants : Taux d’abandon de 12,5 % au cours de l’année scolaire 2025-2026, principalement lié aux difficultés socio-économiques des ménages, aux déplacements forcés, aux travaux domestiques, ainsi qu’aux mariages et grossesses précoces. 131 établissements sur 266 (50 %) rapportent des absences scolaires liées à la gestion des menstruations. 76 responsables d’établissements sur 266 (28%) affirment que les établissements ont subi des pillages ou vols perpétrés par des groupes armés depuis le début de l’année 2026, tandis que 47 sur 266 (18%) ont relevé l’occupation de salles de classe par des forces ou groupes armés. L’inclusion des enfants en situation de handicap demeure limitée, avec peu de mesures spécifiques favorisant leur participation et leur maintien à l’école. Seuls 51 établissements sur 266 (19 %) disposent d’un accès à l’eau potable provenant de leur principale source d’approvisionnement. 114 établissements (43 %) ne disposent pas de latrines séparées pour les filles et les garçons. 101 établissements sur 266 (38 %) signalent la présence d’enfants présentant des signes de détresse psychosociale, notamment des cauchemars, une tristesse persistante, une anxiété élevée, de la fatigue extrême, des comportements violents ou de l’isolement. Seuls 70 établissements sur 266 (26%) disposent d’un mécanisme de référencement VBG adapté aux enfants et permettant l’orientation vers des services spécialisés. Malgré ces défis, les consultations avec les enfants montrent que l’école reste perçue comme un espace de protection, de stabilité et d’espoir. Comme l’a souligné un enfant de 8 à 11 ans : « A l’école, on étudie et on oublie la guerre . »

items.title: Obetsebi Lamptey to Pamprom road to reopen to traffic mid-December – GARID
items.description: The road stretch from the Obetsebi Lamptey Interchange to the Metro Mass area at Pamprom Junction is expected to reopen to motorists between December 15 and 20, 2026, following the completion of 90 per cent of Phase One of the drainage improvement project. Project Manager of the Greater Accra Resilient and Integrated Development (GARID) Project, Cephas Ofori, said the remaining work involved backfilling and restoring the road pavement. Speaking on Channel One News, he said contractors were targeting the mid-December deadline to ease traffic congestion around the interchange during the Christmas season. “We are targeting around the 15th to 20th of December. That is when we are opening the road to the motoring public, from Obetsebi Lamptey through to the Metro Mass area, which we call the Pamprom Crossing,” he said. Mr Ofori explained that the major construction activities, including demolition, excavation, construction of base walls, and installation of cover slabs, had been completed. Meanwhile, work on Phase Two, which extends from the Pamprom Crossing to First Light, has commenced. The westbound carriageway of the Dr Busia Highway from Pamprom Junction was temporarily closed on September 7 to allow major drainage improvement works under the GARID Project. The first phase of the closure was initially scheduled to end in November. GARID Project Communications Specialist, Philip Dunyo, said public education and the provision of alternative routes had helped manage traffic around the construction area. He said motorists had largely complied with the traffic management arrangements introduced before and after the closure, helping to prevent major gridlock and keep traffic moving.

items.title: Incendie au projet ZACA : Le ministre de la Sécurité appelle au respect des normes de transport des produits dangereux‎
items.description: ‎Le ministre de la Sécurité, Mahamadou Sana s'est rendu le vendredi 20 novembre 2026 sur le site de l'incendie survenu au projet ZACA à Ouagadougou le 19 novembre dernier, a fait savoir la Direction de la communication du ministère de la sécurité. À cette occasion, il a appelé les populations et les acteurs économiques au respect strict des normes de conditionnement, de stockage et de transport des marchandises dangereuses. ‎Selon les premières constatations, l'incendie, déclaré le jeudi dernier aux environs de 19 heures serait lié à des insecticides mal conditionnés et non à des explosifs. Aucun décès n'a été enregistré, mais les dégâts sont essentiellement matériels. ‎ ‎Après avoir constaté les dégâts, le ministre a instruit les services compétents de renforcer la sensibilisation des populations sur les bonnes pratiques de manipulation et de conservation des matières dangereuses. Cette sensibilisation passera notamment par la diffusion de capsules de communication. Mahamadou Sana a aussi annoncé un renforcement des contrôles sur le terrain, avec l'implication de la Brigade Laabal, afin d'assainir les marchés et de prévenir la survenue de tels incidents. ‎ ‎Lefaso.net ‎Source : DCRP-MSECU.

items.title: Beach soccer : l'équipe du Maroc dévoile sa liste de 15 joueurs pour la CAN
items.description: La sélection nationale A de beach soccer poursuit ses préparatifs au Complexe Mohammed VI de football, situé dans la périphérie de Salé, en prévision de sa participation à la phase finale de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (CAN), prévue dans la ville de Saly, au Sénégal, du 28 novembre au 6 décembre prochains. Le sélectionneur de l’équipe nationale marocaine de beach soccer, le Brésilien Marcos Octavio, a convoqué 15 joueurs pour prendre part à cette compétition. Parmi eux figurent 12 éléments ayant récemment contribué au sacre du Maroc lors de la Coupe arabe, disputée en Égypte, auxquels s’ajoutent trois nouveaux joueurs choisis pour renforcer l’effectif. Le Maroc disputera son premier match de la phase de groupes face au Malawi, le 29 novembre courant, à partir de 16h30 (heure marocaine). Il affrontera ensuite l’Angola, le 1er décembre prochain à 12h00, avant de croiser la Mauritanie le 2 décembre à partir de 15h00. Les trois rencontres s’inscrivent dans le cadre du groupe B. items.title: La lluvia traiciona a Marc Márquez, que se cae a una vuelta y media de rematar el título en la ‘sprint’ del GP de Portugal
items.description: El piloto español de Ducati, Marc Márquez , se quedó a vuelta y media de proclamarse campeón del mundo este sábado. El catalán se cayó cuando rodaba en tercera posición y la fina lluvia que asomó tímidamente unos pocos minutos durante la carrera comenzó a arreciar con algo más de fuerza en el tramo final. El 93 tenía el título a tocar, pues le sacaba a su rival directo, Jorge Martín, las posiciones necesarias para cantar el alirón ya en la carrera al sprint . Pero tendrá que aguardar al menos hasta mañana, durante la prueba larga del GP de Portugal que se disputa en el circuito de Portimao, donde dispondrá de su tercera bola de campeonato este curso partiendo desde la segunda posición de parrilla: será campeón siempre que sea noveno o mejor, también si queda peor clasificado y no brillan en primera o segunda plaza los dos contrincantes que apenas resisten en la batalla por el título, el propio Martín y Marco Bezzecchi. items.title: India's Congress warns of more protests against Meta after clashes with police outside its offices
items.description: The youth wing of India’s main opposition Congress party on Saturday warned of more protests against Meta’s removal of some accounts and posts of its members, a day after clashing with police outside the US firm’s India offices. Meta declined to comment on Friday’s unprecedented protests, which marked an escalation by the influential political group in the company’s biggest market by users. Debate is growing in India about potential risks to free speech from the increasingly strict efforts of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government to remove social media content it objects to. Modi’s government says it orders content to be taken down only if it breaches local laws, can harm public safety or national security. Congress has long accused Meta and other social media platforms of curbing dissent online by removing party accounts, favouring Modi’s government. Meta has said it restricts content in India to comply with local laws. In Hyderabad on Friday, protesters carrying placards chanted slogans as they stormed into the building that houses Meta’s offices, smashing plants to the ground and clashing with police, according to footage released by the Indian Youth Congress’ X account. Another video showed Congress workers spray-painting anti-Meta slogans on walls outside the building that houses its Mumbai office, clashing with security guards who tried to stop them. In Gurugram near New Delhi, Congress workers chanted slogans and held banners reading “restore youth Congress accounts”, official online posts showed. The Indian Youth Congress posted warnings on X that it would “storm your offices across the country and stage protests” unless Instagram accounts of its leaders are restored. On Saturday, the Congress wing posted a video of its workers putting up a banner in central Delhi taking a dig at Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, referring to him as “Mark BJPberg” to allege the company’s favouritism towards Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party. India’s IT ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Modi’s party accuses congress of vandalism Telangana opposition politician K.T. Rama Rao criticised Congress workers over what he called vandalism at Meta’s Hyderabad office, saying it had undermined the city’s reputation as a safe destination for businesses. Pradeep Bhandari, a national spokesperson for Modi’s ruling party, criticised Congress’ actions on Saturday, saying they had “not only vandalised and destroyed Meta’s office in Hyderabad” but were also “flaunting it on social media”. “This is Congress Model: Vandalise offices of Private companies,” he wrote. Two such accounts were restored after Friday’s protests, but thousands of accounts of journalists, creators and influencers critical of the government remain restricted, Manu Jain, who is in charge of social media for the youth group, told Reuters on Saturday. Meta must explain how its algorithms restrict posts and must restore accounts taken down on government orders, he added. Reporters Without Borders has said the removal of journalistic content from social media has been on the rise in India this year, and free speech activists say a new government rule gives social media companies hardly any time to review and decide on takedown requests. In February, Modi’s government ordered social media companies to take down unlawful content within three hours of being notified about it, tightening an earlier 36-hour timeline. Meta disclosures show that it restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts in India under local laws in the first half of 2026, second only to Indonesia and up from about 70,000 in the whole of 2025. “The large majority of these items included instances where we were obligated to proactively restrict content … based on local law requirements,” Meta said.

items.title: Ndiassane : Ahmadou Alhaminou Lô reçu par les autorités religieuses
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Ahmadou Alhaminou Lô, a été reçu ce samedi à Ndiassane par les autorités religieuses, au nom du Khalife général, Serigne Cheikh Bou Sidy Makhtar Kounta. Cette visite s'inscrit dans le cadre d'une tournée du chef du gouvernement auprès des foyers religieux du pays. NDIASSANE- Il était accompagné d'une forte délégation comprenant notamment le ministre de l'Intérieur et de la Sécurité publique, le ministre de l'Industrie et du Commerce, le Délégué général aux Affaires religieuses, les autorités administratives de la région de Thiès ainsi que le directeur général du quotidien national Le Soleil. Le chef du gouvernement a été accueilli avec tous les honneurs par le porte-parole du Khalife et les membres de la famille Kountiyou de Ndiassane et des localités environnantes. Prenant la parole, il a transmis aux autorités religieuses les salutations du président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye. « Nous sommes venus, au nom du chef de l'État, recueillir les préoccupations des foyers religieux », a déclaré Mouhamadou Alaminou Lo. Il a rappelé, à cette occasion, la création de la Délégation générale aux Affaires religieuses, annoncée à Ndiassane, pour illustrer l'importance que le président de la République accorde à cette cité religieuse. En réponse aux préoccupations soulevées par le chef de village, le Premier ministre a assuré que le gouvernement veillera à leur prise en charge dans différents secteurs, notamment l'éducation, la santé et les infrastructures routières. Il a indiqué que toutes les dispositions avaient été prises pour permettre l'exécution des budgets prévus. Concernant les bourses de sécurité familiale, il a annoncé que leur paiement avait démarré et se poursuivrait conformément aux prévisions budgétaires. Ahlaminou Lô a également assuré que les budgets de la loi de finances rectificative (LFR) 2026 et de la loi de finances initiale (LFI) 2027 étaient en place et seraient exécutés convenablement, avec l'appui des partenaires extérieurs. Il a, par ailleurs, souligné que les opérateurs économiques seraient payés afin de préserver la stabilité de l'économie. Abordant la question des réseaux sociaux, le Premier ministre a dénoncé les dérives qui y sont constatées et annoncé que le gouvernement prendrait les dispositions nécessaires. Il a invité les autorités religieuses à poursuivre leur travail de sensibilisation auprès des populations. « Le Sénégal est un pays de paix et de stabilité et il le restera », a-t-il affirmé. Le chef du gouvernement a enfin sollicité des prières pour la réussite du président de la République et la préservation de la paix et de la stabilité dans le pays. De son côté, Serigne Khalifa Kounta s'est réjoui de la visite du Premier ministre à Ndiassane. Il a rappelé la place de cette cité dans l'islam au Sénégal, ainsi que le rôle important que joue le Khalife général, aux côtés des autres guides religieux, dans la préservation de la stabilité nationale. Le porte-parole du Khalife a également magnifié la contribution du quotidien national Le Soleil à la communication autour du Gamou annuel, depuis l'arrivée de son directeur général, Mouhamadou Lamine Niang. Ibrahima NDIAYE (Correspondant)

items.title: 2027: Reset your mind, align with people’s choice, Oshiomhole tells Makinde
items.description: By Adeola Badru Senator Adams Oshiomhole, former Governor of Edo State, has urged Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, to reconsider his political position ahead of the 2027 general elections, saying the country needed leaders committed to sustaining progress. Oshiomhole, who spoke in Ibadan on Saturday during President Bola Tinubu’s rally at the historic Mapo Hall, challenged Makinde to align himself with the wishes of the electorate, insisting that the governor must first reconsider his own position on Tinubu’s re-election bid. The former Edo governor, who expressed support for Tinubu’s second-term ambition, described the forthcoming election as a decisive moment for Nigeria and questioned whether Makinde’s call for a reset was intended to reverse policies he said had benefited ordinary Nigerians. “This coming election is a decisive factor. We have a leader, the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. Oshiomhole said he had questions for Makinde over his position on Tinubu’s continuation in office, particularly regarding the administration’s student loan scheme, infrastructure development, and improved welfare for university lecturers. He asked whether Makinde’s opposition to the president’s re-election was connected to the federal government’s decision to provide financial assistance to students from poor backgrounds through the student loan scheme. “Is Seyi Makinde angry because Tinubu is giving loans to the children of poor people in our universities? Is that what Makinde wants to reset?” he asked. The senator also questioned whether the governor intended to reverse the federal government’s infrastructure projects, particularly the coastal highway linking Lagos to Calabar, which he said would improve connectivity and make movement easier for Nigerians. “The President is creating massive infrastructure to connect Lagos to Calabar so that our people can move. Is that what Makinde wants to reset?” he said. Oshiomhole further challenged Makinde’s position on the welfare of university lecturers, citing the University of Ibadan as an example of an institution that had previously experienced repeated disruptions to its academic calendar due to industrial action. He recalled that university lecturers had, in the past, frequently embarked on strikes, disrupting academic activities and delaying students’ graduation. “For this city has the most outstanding university in Africa, the University of Ibadan. For a long, long time, the lecturer will teach you for two days and then will go on strike for three days. Is that not true?” he said. The former governor said the Tinubu administration had deliberately prioritized the welfare of university lecturers, whom he described as critical to developing the country’s future workforce. He argued that improved remuneration for lecturers would strengthen the education sector, encourage qualified academics to remain in the profession, and ensure that students could complete their studies without repeated interruptions. “I just want to deliver this message. Now, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has deliberately decided that those who make the manpower of tomorrow are the lecturers in our universities.” “And he has increased their pay substantially so that for four years, your academic calendar has not been interrupted,” he said. Oshiomhole asked whether Makinde intended to reverse the policy, allow strikes to return to the university system, or reduce lecturers’ salaries. “Does Makinde want to reset this policy? Does he want the strike to return? Does he want to reduce the salaries of lecturers?” he asked. He maintained that improved remuneration for university lecturers would encourage more intelligent minds to return to the teaching profession, which he described as one of the noblest professions. “When you pay lecturers very well, intelligent minds will go back to the teaching profession, which is the most noble profession,” he said. Oshiomhole, who repeatedly challenged Makinde’s call for a reset, urged the governor to reconsider his position and align himself with the aspirations of the electorate ahead of the 2027 elections. He said Nigeria needed political leaders who would prioritize the country’s development and sustain policies aimed at improving the lives of citizens. “When you go back, tell the man in Ibadan he is for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. The senator concluded by urging Makinde to reconsider his position before the election, stressing that the country’s progress should remain the priority of political leaders. “The governor needs to reset his own mind before the election. We want Nigeria to progress. Thank you and God bless,” Oshiomhole said The post 2027: Reset your mind, align with people’s choice, Oshiomhole tells Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Capt Safdar seeks Rs10bn in damages from Advocate Mian Dawood over 'defamatory' remarks
items.description: LAHORE: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s spouse and former MNA, retired Capt Muhammad Safdar, has served a legal notice to Advocate Mian Dawood, demanding an unconditional public apology, retraction of allegedly defamatory remarks, removal of videos and Rs10 billion in damages. The notice, dated Nov 20, was issued through a Rawalpindi-based lawyer, Majad Ali Butt, under Section 10 of the Punjab Defamation Act 2024 . Advocate Dawood confirmed to Dawn that he had received the legal notice. He said an appropriate response would be sent to Safdar after examining the notice. According to the notice, the dispute arose from Safdar’s public demand that former president of the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA), Ahsan Bhoon, produce his LLB degree, a matter it says is already before the Supreme Court and the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC). Last month, PBC declared that the degrees of Bhoon and its other elected members were genuine. The notice claimed that Safdar had said he would apologise if Bhoon’s degree proved genuine and that Advocate Dawood, an “unrelated third party”, responded with malice. The notice cited three pieces of content, including a two-minute video uploaded on Sept 24 on YouTube, a news channel interview aired on Oct 29 and a video statement made after the SCBA elections held last month. It argued that free speech cannot become a “licence for vulgar abuse”, and that Dawood was expected to show restraint. The notice demanded that the lawyer publish, within 14 days, an apology on the same platforms and in leading English and Urdu newspapers, retract the statements, have the videos removed, pay Rs10bn and refrain from repeating the remarks. Failing that, Safdar would approach the Special Tribunal under the Defamation Act, the notice warned. In late September, Safdar called for verification of the degrees of prominent lawyers, including Bhoon, a close associate of Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar. His remarks also came ahead of the SCBA elections. Bhoon heads the Independent Group, also known as the Asma Jahangir Group. Safdar had announced the formation of his own group, the Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah Group. Subsequently, Bhoon filed a Rs5 billion defamation suit against Safdar over remarks questioning the authenticity of his LLB degree. The Punjab Defamation Tribunal had admitted the suit for hearing and issued a notice to Safdar. Meanwhile, the retired Captain had moved a complaint with the Judicial Commission of Pakistan to seek verification of Bhoon’s educational qualifications. Days later, PBC said that the returning officers (ROs) for its 2020 and 2025 elections had gotten the elected members’ degrees verified from their respective universities before notifying them as the council’s members.

items.title: Oyo rally: Tinubu assures Nigerians of improved electricity supply
items.description: President Bola Tinubu has assured Nigerians of improved electricity supply, stressing that his administration is working round the clock to boost the power sector. The president stated this on Saturday in Ibadan during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign held at the historic Mapo Hall. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the event also featured the formal presentation by President Tinubu of Sen. Sharafadeen Alli as the APC’s governorship candidate to the party’s supporters in Oyo State. Tinubu commended Oyo State for the overwhelming votes delivered to him in the 2023 elections and urged the citizens to see the party as their own. “For the sake of progress, development, your children’s future, and prosperity for our country, I urge you to stay the course. “For our children and grandchildren to benefit from the hope of Nigeria, we must give them the right education and invest in agriculture. “For Oyo State, we just signed an agreement with Yutong Automobile of China to reopen the old Leyland Automobile factory in Ibadan. “This aims to start production of commercial vehicles and commence general automobile assembly plant. “We will continue to bring in more industry, and, in addition, I guarantee you improvement in electricity supply,” he said. The president, while commending the support of traditional rulers and leaders of the party in the state, urged supporters not to be deceived by other parties that allegedly come to dupe them. Earlier, in separate goodwill messages, the governor of Ekiti State, Mr. Biodun Oyebanji, on behalf of the 31 progressive governors, and the Anambra and Osun governors, urged the electorate in Yoruba not to trade their votes. This, he said, was necessary to let the president continue his reforms and good works, such as student loan initiatives, infrastructural development, and various transformational moves in other sectors. Also, the Senate Leader, Sen. Opeyemi Bamidele, said that splitting the APC votes for different parties across different political offices in Oyo State would not profit the party maximally. He stressed that votes for the presidential, governorship, and national and state assemblies should be for the APC. Bamidele added that the achievements of the president in the last three years should be the template for the campaign. Also, Sen. Adams Oshiomhole said that the coming election remained a decisive factor, as various initiatives and reforms of the president were already resetting Nigeria and should not be a campaign slogan for any other candidate. NAN reports that the campaign was attended by both former and serving governors, their wives, members of the Senate and House of Representatives, and party leaders, among others. (NAN) The post Oyo rally: Tinubu assures Nigerians of improved electricity supply appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Octobre Rose 2026 : le Crédit Rural de Guinée mobilisé pour la sensibilisation et le dépistage du cancer du sein
items.description: Le Crédit Rural de Guinée (CRG) a organisé, du 22 au 24 octobre 2026, trois journées de sensibilisation au cancer du sein dans le cadre de la campagne Octobre Rose. Baptisée « CRG EN ROSE 2026 », cette initiative, placée sous le thème « Ensemble pour la santé de nos femmes », visait à informer les femmes sur la maladie et à encourager le dépistage précoce. La campagne a été marquée par des séances d’information animées avec la participation d’un médecin spécialiste, ainsi que par le témoignage d’une femme ayant subi une intervention chirurgicale liée à la maladie. Les échanges ont été conduits dans plusieurs langues afin de faciliter la compréhension des messages de prévention. Les équipes du CRG se sont également rendues dans différents marchés pour sensibiliser directement les femmes, répondre à leurs préoccupations et les informer sur les possibilités de dépistage. L'institution a notamment contribué à leur orientation vers les centres de santé et facilité leurs déplacements pour accéder aux services de dépistage. À travers cette mobilisation, le Crédit Rural de Guinée entend inscrire son engagement au-delà de ses activités de microfinance, en participant aux initiatives de santé publique. L'institution met ainsi l'accent sur l'information, la prévention et l'accès au dépistage précoce, des leviers essentiels dans la lutte contre le cancer du sein. items.title: Raffinage : trois scénarios pour sortir de l’après-Samir
items.description: Dix ans après l’arrêt de la raffinerie de Mohammedia, le Centre de prospective économique et sociale (CPES) estime que le Royaume n’a pas à choisir entre nostalgie et statu quo. Son rapport passe en revue trois voies, de la remise en marche de Samir à la construction d’un site neuf, et plaide pour une évaluation nationale indépendante avant tout arbitrage. Depuis 2015, le Maroc couvre la totalité de ses besoins en produits pétroliers par des importations. Cette dépendance, devenue structurelle, pèse sur les comptes extérieurs et expose le pays aux soubresauts des marchés internationaux. Dans un rapport consacré au raffinage, le CPES refuse pourtant de réduire le débat à la seule renaissance de Samir. Pour ses auteurs, la question est d’abord stratégique : quelle part de la chaîne de valeur énergétique le Royaume veut-il maîtriser, à quel coût et avec quelles garanties de rentabilité ? Trois options sont mises sur la table, chacune avec ses atouts et ses angles morts. L’arrêt du raffinage a, selon le rapport, mis au jour des fragilités économiques et structurelles durables. La première est budgétaire : la facture énergétique reste lourde, même si elle s’est allégée, passant d’environ 113,98 milliards de dirhams en 2024 à 107,56 milliards en 2025. Les fluctuations des cours mondiaux se transmettent ensuite directement aux coûts de production, au transport et aux prix des biens et services, ce qui grignote le pouvoir d’achat des ménages, en particulier celui des foyers modestes et de la classe moyenne. S’y ajoutent la perte d’une partie de la valeur ajoutée industrielle ainsi que des investissements et des emplois que cette activité générait. Le CPES rappelle l’ordre de grandeur de ce qui a disparu. Avec une capacité de conception d’environ 200 000 barils par jour, soit près de 10 millions de tonnes par an, Samir pouvait répondre à quelque 78 % de la consommation nationale de produits pétroliers, établie à 12,867 millions de tonnes en 2025. Sa mise à l’arrêt a placé le pays face à un double risque extérieur, celui du prix du brut et celui du prix, comme de la disponibilité, des produits raffinés. Elle a aussi privé le Maroc d’environ deux millions de mètres cubes de capacités de stockage, un handicap pour absorber une rupture d’approvisionnement ou une crise géopolitique. Le premier scénario consiste à réhabiliter et relancer l’outil de Mohammedia. Il présente l’avantage de s’appuyer sur des actifs existants plutôt que de repartir de zéro. Mais la facture de remise à niveau dépasserait 350 millions de dollars selon certaines estimations, un montant à distinguer du prix d’acquisition des actifs. Il faudra surtout démêler les obstacles juridiques et financiers liés à la liquidation judiciaire et trouver un investisseur, ce qui fait de ce retour une affaire bien plus complexe qu’une simple décision politique. Le deuxième scénario porte sur une raffinerie neuve, d’une capacité de 100 000 à 150 000 barils par jour. Elle permettrait de concevoir un site moderne, conforme aux normes techniques et environnementales actuelles, calibré sur la demande nationale et implanté au meilleur endroit. En contrepartie, le ticket d’entrée serait considérable. Il faudrait sécuriser un approvisionnement régulier en brut, signer des contrats de commercialisation et résister à la concurrence des grandes raffineries étrangères. Le rapport invite aussi à anticiper l’évolution de la demande de carburants à l’heure de l’essor des énergies renouvelables, afin d’éviter de se retrouver avec une installation lourde, aux coûts fixes élevés, face à un marché en mutation. Le troisième scénario mise sur la continuité, en perfectionnant le modèle fondé sur l’importation de produits raffinés. Il suppose de diversifier les fournisseurs, d’améliorer les conditions contractuelles, d’étendre le stockage, de moderniser les infrastructures portuaires et logistiques et de renforcer la transparence et la concurrence sur le marché intérieur. Le pays dispose déjà des moyens de continuer à s’approvisionner ainsi, sans supporter le coût d’une nouvelle usine. Ce choix reste toutefois exposé aux prix internationaux ainsi qu’aux marges de raffinage et de transport, qui se constituent hors de l’économie nationale, et il n’apporte aucune réponse à la question de la souveraineté industrielle. Le CPES le juge praticable à court et moyen terme, mais insuffisant à lui seul. Au terme de la comparaison, le centre écarte l’idée d’un choix purement technique. Il s’agit d’arbitrer entre coût financier, rentabilité, sécurité énergétique et capacité à créer de la valeur. Relancer Samir repose sur des actifs tangibles, mais reste suspendu aux résultats de l’expertise technique, à la clarification juridique et au financement. Bâtir du neuf offre la technologie la plus récente, au prix d’investissements plus élevés et de délais plus longs. Continuer d’importer procure de la souplesse à court terme, tout en pérennisant la dépendance et la perte de valeur ajoutée. La voie jugée la plus réaliste est donc celle d’une approche composite, qui commence par une évaluation nationale indépendante et globale de l’avenir du raffinage. En attendant que l’option industrielle soit tranchée, le rapport recommande de poursuivre le programme de stockage stratégique, de tirer le meilleur parti des réservoirs disponibles, de diversifier les sources d’approvisionnement, de moderniser les infrastructures portuaires et logistiques et de renforcer la transparence comme la concurrence sur le marché des carburants. La politique de raffinage et de stockage devrait en outre s’inscrire dans la stratégie énergétique d’ensemble. L’objectif, souligne le CPES, n’est pas de ressusciter le modèle d’hier, mais d’édifier un système énergétique plus sûr et plus compétitif, qui combine diversification des sources, maintien d’une capacité nationale de raffinage, développement du stockage et récupération d’une partie de la valeur ajoutée industrielle sur le sol marocain. The post Raffinage : trois scénarios pour sortir de l’après-Samir appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: EU proposes tax on Big Tech to boost budget
items.description: The European Union (EU) put forward plans on Saturday to tax the world’s biggest digital companies to fund its next budget, as it seeks to bridge divisions among member states over the bloc’s long-term funding. European Council President Antonio Costa unveiled a new spending proposal that slashes by €204 billion ($224bn) a plan initially put forward by the European Commission, which some countries had slammed as too onerous. “I believe this proposal can bring us closer to a final agreement,” Costa told a press conference in Brussels. But the draft immediately drew criticism both from so-called “frugal” EU members led by Germany and those like France opposing large cuts. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the budget’s “overall size remains too high”, noting that “virtually all” member states had to consolidate public finances at home. French President Emmanuel Macron’s office instead slammed the proposal as “disappointing”, notably for what concerned income support for farmers. EU nations have been squabbling over the size of the next budget, with Germany leading calls for major cuts after the commission last year proposed a €2-trillion budget for the 2028-2034 period. Digital tax Costa, who represents the EU’s 27 states, is seeking to reach a deal by the end of the year balancing contributions from member states with new sources of revenue for the bloc. Among these could be a tax on digital firms, which the draft Costa presented on Saturday says will concern companies with an annual turnover for digital activities of at least €50 million in the EU as well as a global turnover of more than €750m. They would be subjected to “an annual contribution corresponding to 3 per cent of the annual net turnover from online advertising, digital intermediation services and user-generated data”, according to documents shared by the council. The plan is likely to provoke United States President Donald Trump’s ire since his administration has reacted angrily to EU fines and moves against Big Tech under its content and competition rules in recent years. “This tax is in no way directed against any particular company or country,” Costa said of the levy, which replaces a charge on large companies envisaged by the commission. The draft also includes plans for a levy on electronic waste and higher tobacco taxes. Costa said the EU will explore a tax on crypto assets and to gain revenue from radio spectrum auctions. Overall, the council estimates the EU’s “own resources” could generate about 60 billion euros in revenue each year. Parliament threat The draft will be at the centre of fraught talks when EU leaders meet in Brussels next week. Costa is pushing for a deal in December, amid EU fears that a delay would push talks into a fraught election year in 2027, with worries about what potential eurosceptic victories in France and elsewhere would mean for future dealmaking. Once EU states find an agreement, they will have to negotiate with parliament — a task that also promises to be difficult. “President Costa’s proposal is simply unacceptable. The Council is fixated on cuts when Europe needs ambition and resources to tackle its mounting challenges,” key budget lawmaker Siegfried Muresan warned. Costa does not only have to contend with the frugals’ demands. France, the second-biggest EU economy and a net contributor to the budget, argues the bloc needs sufficient means to match the rising challenges it faces. Meanwhile, 17 countries from southern, central and eastern Europe have formed a group known as the “Friends of Cohesion” and are pushing for greater funding to support agriculture and regional development. “We are still a long way from a compromise,” Jessica Rosencrantz, Europe Minister of Sweden, which is with Germany among five nations pushing to cut back national contributions, wrote on X.

items.title: Algérie : 17 narcotrafiquants arrêtés, 1,9 tonne de kif traité marocain saisie
items.description: L’Armée nationale populaire a porté un nouveau coup dur contre les réseaux de trafic de drogues en Algérie. Cette fois, ses services de sécurité ont réalisé une opération spectaculaire et mis la main sur une somme de 2,73 millions de dinars. « Dans la poursuite des efforts visant à lutter et à resserrer l’étau sur les narcotrafiquants, et grâce à une coordination sécuritaire rigoureuse, les services de la Sécurité de l’Armée en 2°Région Militaire ont démantelé, au cours de cette semaine, un réseau de narcotrafiquants qui tentait d’introduire une quantité importante de kif traité en provenance du Maroc, estimée à 19 quintaux », a annoncé le ministère de la Défense nationale ce samedi 21 novembre. L’ANP multiplie les opérations anti-drogue Cette opération a également permis « l’arrestation de 17 narcotrafiquants et la saisie de 50 véhicules utilitaires, cinq motocyclettes, un jet-ski, des téléphones portables ainsi qu’une somme d’argent estimée à 273 millions de centimes », a précisé le MDN. « Ces résultats qualitatifs sur le terrain viennent réaffirmer, encore une fois, la détermination et la résolution des unités de l’Armée Nationale Populaire à poursuivre avec fermeté la lutte contre toutes les formes de contrebande et de criminalité organisée », a ajouté la même source. Vendredi, les Garde-frontières algériens ont abattu deux narcotrafiquants marocains dans la région de Naâma, près de la bande frontalière ouest. Les deux trafiquants ont « refusé d’obtempérer, alors qu’ils tentaient d’introduire sur le territoire national une quantité de kif traité s’élevant à plus de 50 kilogrammes », a précisé le MDN. items.title: Zelensky reaffirms Ukraine’s wish to join NATO
items.description: Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky on Saturday reiterated his country’s determination to join NATO, following proposals to provide Kyiv with security guarantees similar to those of the military alliance. “Of course Ukraine very much wants to be in NATO,” Zelensky told reporters, judging that membership of the alliance was one of the “most obvious security guarantees” for his country. The issue of Ukraine joining NATO, ruled out by Washington since 2025, resurfaced in recent days during fresh talks to end the war nearly five years after Russia’s invasion. At a meeting with Kyiv’s allies in Berlin on Thursday, US envoy Jared Kushner said Washington could be ready to grant Ukraine a security guarantee similar to that provided under Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty. That clause – the cornerstone of NATO – states that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all allies. On Friday, the French presidency said offering Kyiv “Article 5-type” protection would in practice amount to bringing Ukraine into the alliance. The same day, two Russian missiles and a suspected drone landed in southeastern Poland, a NATO member bordering Ukraine. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte denounced violations of Polish airspace, calling them “clearly dangerous”. items.title: Ghana to vote for Infantino’s re-election as all 54 CAF nations back FIFA president
items.description: Ghana will vote for Gianni Infantino in the March 2027 FIFA presidential election after all 54 member associations of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), including the Ghana Football Association (GFA), unanimously endorsed the incumbent for another term. CAF president Patrice Motsepe confirmed the collective backing at the 48th CAF Ordinary General Assembly in Abuja, Nigeria, on Saturday, 21 November 2026. Motsepe said all 54 African football associations had formally submitted documents pledging their support for Infantino ahead of the election, which will take place on 18 March 2027 in Rabat, Morocco. “The decision that CAF took in Cabo Verde and the decision we took even before that to express the unanimous support of the 54 African nations, I keep saying to Gianni Infantino,” Motsepe stated. “I have these documents with me. I have a report from all 54 member associations in Africa to say that we’re unanimously supporting Gianni.” Ghana’s backing forms part of the continent-wide endorsement, giving Infantino the support of all 54 African votes as he seeks to extend his leadership of world football’s governing body. The FIFA president succeeded Sepp Blatter in February 2016 and is seeking another mandate at the 77th FIFA Congress in Morocco. Nigeria had earlier reaffirmed its support for Infantino, with the country’s backing reportedly communicated directly by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. However, Infantino could face competition from French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo and former Japan Football Association president Kohzo Tashima, both of whom have submitted their intentions to contest the election. Their candidacies, alongside other applications, remain subject to examination by FIFA’s electoral committee to determine whether they meet the required eligibility criteria. The final list of proposed and admitted candidates is expected to be communicated to FIFA member associations by 18 February 2027. The election will be held in Rabat, Morocco, on 18 March 2027, with representatives of FIFA’s member associations voting to determine the organisation’s leadership for the next presidential term. With Ghana and the other 53 African associations behind him, Infantino has secured a significant bloc of support ahead of the election, although the final outcome will be determined by FIFA’s member associations worldwide.

items.title: TikTok refuse un projet de structure de propriété européenne pour ses activités
items.description: La plateforme de vidéos TikTok a rejeté une initiative de l'Allemagne et de l'Autriche visant à placer ses activités européennes sous une structure de propriété européenne, qualifiant cette proposition d'“absurde”, rapporte samedi la presse allemande. Citée par plusieurs médias, une porte-parole de TikTok a déclaré que la plateforme était déjà soumise à la législation européenne, qui encadre notamment la protection des données et les activités des entreprises numériques. La société a également fait valoir que cette initiative ne tenait pas compte de son programme d'investissement de 12 milliards d'euros dans la protection des données, qui comprend notamment des centres de stockage en Europe. Mercredi, le ministre allemand délégué à la Culture et aux Médias, Wolfram Weimer, et le secrétaire d'État autrichien chargé du Numérique, Alexander Pröll, avaient proposé de créer une structure de propriété européenne pour les activités de TikTok sur le continent, tout en plaçant ses principales infrastructures technologiques sous responsabilité européenne. Les deux responsables ont justifié cette initiative par des préoccupations liées à la protection des données personnelles, aux risques d'ingérence étrangère et à l'influence des plateformes numériques sur l'opinion publique. Propriété du groupe chinois ByteDance, TikTok compte environ 200 millions d'utilisateurs mensuels en Europe. items.title: Black Challenge: Assafuah blasts Sports Minister Kofi Adams over alleged neglect of Amputee World Cup finalists
items.description: Old Tafo MP and Ranking Member of Parliament’s Youth and Sports Committee, Vincent Ekow Assafuah, has criticised Sports Minister Kofi Adams over the Ministry’s handling of Ghana’s Black Challenge during their historic campaign at the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. Assafuah accused the Minister of neglecting the national amputee football team, questioning why the government had not given the players the financial attention and support they deserved despite representing Ghana on the global stage. In a Facebook post, the MP recalled visiting the team on October 24, 2026, before their departure for Mexico to encourage the players and wish them well. He questioned the Ministry’s apparent lack of involvement during the competition, asking whether the team’s circumstances would have been different had they been the Black Stars. “Why has the Minister neglected this team? Is it because they are not the Black Stars?” he queried. His criticism follows revelations that the Black Challenge played five consecutive matches without receiving their daily allowances and winning bonuses from the state, prompting appeals from players and technical team members. Technical team member Ali Jaraah had also questioned whether the Minister would associate himself with the team’s achievements should they win the tournament. Assafuah further challenged Adams over the timing of his public recognition of the team, insisting that government support should extend beyond celebrating their achievements. “You cannot abandon a team in its moment of preparation and suddenly become part of its success story when the medals arrive,” he wrote. The Minister has since praised the team, explaining that an agreement with Gold Fields Ghana would provide US$8,000 per member of the delegation to cover approved per diems and match bonuses. The Black Challenge have reached their first-ever World Cup final after defeating defending champions Türkiye on penalties and will face Morocco for the title.

items.title: Outrage as Defence Ministry publicises APC campaign rally
items.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Ministry of Defence has come under criticism on social media after its official X account published details of preparations for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in support of President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid. In a post on Saturday, it announced that the rally was scheduled to hold at Mapo Hall, Ibadan, Oyo State, on November 21, 2026, with Tinubu and key party officials expected to attend. It also disclosed that the Minister of Defence, retired General Christopher Musa, had visited the venue on Friday night to assess security arrangements and other preparations ahead of the event. “Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), OFR, Friday night conducted an on-the-spot inspection of the venue as part of strategic preparations ahead of the upcoming presidential campaign rally in the state,” the post reads. “During the visit, General Musa toured the premises and surrounding perimeters to evaluate security readiness, crowd management logistics, and overall infrastructural preparedness. President Bola Tinubu GCFR, and key party officials would be on ground for the rally.” Defence Ministry/X Defence Ministry/X The post, which was accompanied by photographs of the minister’s inspection, was followed by criticism from several Nigerians, who questioned the use of an official government platform to publicise the activities of a political party. One of the critics, Kunle Adebajo, described the development as “political psychosis so deep it’s ridiculous even by Nigerian standards”. Another X user, N6, questioned the ministry’s apparent involvement in partisan activities, asking, “How is the Ministry of Defence handle clearly being Partisan. Have you lost it?” Similarly, a user identified as Dollarain2000 said, “Is this really the official handle of Nigeria’s Defence Ministry? Or the Security Directorate of the APC Presidential Campaign Council?” the user asked. Another critic, Emmanuel Doji, expressed concern over what he described as the blurring of boundaries between government responsibilities and involvement in partisan political activities. He wrote, “So what exactly is the meaning of this? The official Twitter handle of the Ministry of Defence is now publishing a political party’s campaign schedule and updates on preparations for its rally? Where exactly do we draw the line between government business and party politics? “A whole Ministry of Defence is now a publicity arm of the APC. Will it also publish the activities and campaign schedules of other political parties? This is completely inappropriate and should be condemned. Government institutions should not be turned into platforms for partisan political activities. This is not how things should be done.” Another user, Benjamin, wrote, “Defence handle of the nation doing this! No, no, no, no! This is preposterous! This is no more Democracy!” Josephu_o also criticised the development, he wrote, “Imagine the Ministry of Defence, an institution funded by Nigerian taxpayers and entrusted with the security of over 200 million citizens, using its official platform to publicise a political party’s re-election rally. “Is this a Ministry of Defence or an APC campaign publicity office? State institutions belong to Nigerians, not political parties,” the user added. Another user, HonShield, questioned whether the ministry would extend the same publicity to opposition parties, asking, “Dear Ministry of Defence, will you also do this for other political parties? Do you now belong to the APC to be tweeting for their campaign? What’s going on in this country for God’s sake?” The post Outrage as Defence Ministry publicises APC campaign rally appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Israeli strike on vehicle in Gaza kills three, Gaza Health Ministry says
items.description: JERUSALEM, Nov 21 (Reuters) - Israeli forces hit a truck in Gaza on Saturday which witnesses said was carrying food and papers bearing the logo of the World Central Kitchen charity, but the organisation said the vehicle was not affiliated with it. items.title: Haaland in VAR controversy as Man City held by Fulham
items.description: Erling Haaland was controversially denied a crucial goal as Manchester City’s spluttering Premier League title challenge suffered a fresh blow in a 1-1 draw against Fulham on Saturday. Enzo Maresca’s side trailed to Rodrigo Muniz’s early opener at the Etihad Stadium before Haaland’s equaliser was contentiously ruled out. The City striker kicked the ball out of the grasp of Fulham keeper Bernd Leno on the goal-line. But Leno barely had two hands on the ball when Haaland made contact, giving City reason to feel aggrieved with the decision. Elliot Anderson saved City from a fourth successive league defeat as the England midfielder equalised in the second half with his first top-flight goal since signing from Nottingham Forest in the close-season. But it was another frustrating afternoon for third-placed City, who could not find a winner and were booed off at full-time. Leaders Arsenal can extend their lead over City to eight points if they win at Newcastle later on Saturday. After making a blistering start to the season with seven successive league wins, City are winless in their last four top-flight matches. It was the first time in 15 years and 21 games that City had failed to beat Fulham. Still waiting to discover the result of their appeal against the guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules, City have looked increasingly distracted in recent weeks. Maresca has claimed City are not bothered by the “noise” around the financial scandal, which is likely to include a huge points deduction if the appeal fails. But his team’s lethargic performances of late suggest otherwise, with tricky tests against Napoli on Tuesday and Arsenal next weekend threatening to extend their slump. – Slumping City – City needed a fast start to ease their anxiety and Erling Haaland almost delivered it when his looping header was cleared off the line. But Maresca has failed to fix the defensive problems that ailed City in their previous three games. Fulham took full advantage of City’s flaws to snatch the lead with an incisive counter in the 16th minute. Former City winger Oscar Bobb pounced on a wayward pass and accelerated down the right flank before picking out Muniz’s run into the penalty area. With City’s defence in disarray, Muniz kept his composure to curl a fine finish into the top corner. Maresca turned away in disgust and his frustration only increased when City were denied a leveller in the 26th minute. Iliman Ndiaye’s cross reached Haaland inside the six-yard box but the Norway striker’s weak volley was saved by Leno. Haaland’s momentum carried him into Leno and he kicked the ball over the line as the Fulham keeper struggled to get hold of it. But Haaland’s celebrations were curtailed by VAR’s decision to disallow the goal for a foul on Leno. Haaland squandered a golden opportunity to drag City level when he blazed wildly over from Phil Foden’s defence splitting pass. Enduring one of his more profligate days, Haaland scuffed wastefully wide from Nico O’Reilly’s pass. Out of sync for so long, City finally found some rhythm after the break and their pressure was rewarded in the 58th minute. Fulham failed to clear a corner and Anderson pounced, drilling a fierce volley past Leno from the edge of the area. Anderson was inches away from putting City ahead moments later with a low drive that fizzes just wide. It was that kind of day for City, whose season is in danger of spiralling out of control before they even discover their appeal verdict. items.title: Ghanaian cyclist takes climate campaign to COP31, calls for youth-led environmental action
items.description: For five years, James Kumbeni has turned his bicycle into an instrument of climate advocacy, cycling across communities to promote environmental awareness and encourage action against carbon emissions. The Ghanaian climate campaigner has now taken that mission beyond the country’s borders, arriving at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, with his bicycle and a renewed determination to inspire environmental action. For Kumbeni, the journey to COP31 is more than an opportunity to participate in global climate discussions. It is a chance to learn, build partnerships, and strengthen the campaign he has been pursuing through cycling in Ghana. “This is my first COP and the knowledge I have come here to get is massive. The connections I’ve also made here and all the ideas, I know going back, all these ones are going to shape the way and how I do my climate change campaign in Ghana,” he said in an interview with JoyNews. Kumbeni’s participation has also extended to discussions on youth engagement in environmental sustainability. At a panel discussion on “Tree Planting and Young People: The Global South Approach,” he called for greater inclusion of young people in climate decision-making, investment in their capacity development and accessible financing for youth-led environmental initiatives. He argued that young people should not merely be mobilised to participate in environmental campaigns but must be empowered to influence decisions and implement solutions. He also challenged stakeholders to move beyond tree-planting exercises that focus largely on the number of seedlings planted, insisting that greater attention must be given to their survival and long-term environmental impact. According to him, effective monitoring systems are needed to track the growth of planted trees, ensure their survival and assess their actual contribution to environmental restoration. Kumbeni further called for climate solutions that reflect the realities of the Global South, emphasising the importance of indigenous knowledge, local environmental conditions and the specific development challenges confronting communities. The Ghanaian cyclist says his participation in COP31 has broadened his understanding of climate action, particularly in areas such as carbon markets, tree-planting initiatives and international partnerships. He believes the knowledge acquired could help expand his advocacy work when he returns home. “Some of the things I’ve learned include carbon markets. Since I’ve been doing carbon emissions and all that, having come here to learn about carbon markets means that when I go home, I should be able to do something around carbon markets,” he explained. He also hopes to improve the design and implementation of tree-planting activities to ensure that seedlings are properly nurtured and grow to maturity. Beyond the technical knowledge, Kumbeni considers the relationships established at COP31 an important resource for scaling up his work. He believes partnerships with individuals and organisations will help mobilise the expertise and resources needed to achieve greater environmental impact. “Partnerships help you to pull resources together to make a much bigger impact,” he said. Kumbeni’s participation at COP31 has also exposed him to opportunities for promoting sustainable mobility, particularly the development of cycling infrastructure. Comparing the cycling environment in Türkiye with conditions in Ghana, he says the availability of dedicated cycling lanes and greater consideration for cyclists by motorists are important lessons for his country. He wants Ghana to begin a broader conversation about providing safer spaces for cyclists and encouraging more people to use bicycles for commuting and other daily activities. However, he believes infrastructure development must be accompanied by public education to improve how motorists share the road with cyclists. “Another big thing too is that at places where there are no cycling lanes, the drivers are usually patient. When I was cycling to this particular place, you don’t hear drivers honking at you, and they would usually give you a safe distance so that you don’t get knocked down,” he observed. He said Ghana could begin by intensifying road safety education and promoting mutual respect between motorists and cyclists, even as authorities work towards developing dedicated cycling lanes. According to him, making roads safer would encourage more people to embrace cycling, helping to reduce emissions associated with motorised transportation. Kumbeni says his five-year cycling campaign has contributed to environmental protection in several ways. By undertaking his journeys on a bicycle rather than using a motor vehicle, he believes he has avoided thousands of kilograms of carbon emissions. “The impact has been great. This is my fifth year cycling for climate change. On my own movements, I have been able to save the environment from pollution, considering that all these trips I have been embarking on are always on a bicycle, not a motor vehicle,” he said. He added that several people had acquired bicycles and started riding after being inspired by his campaign. Despite the challenges of promoting cycling and environmental awareness in Ghana, Kumbeni remains optimistic about the prospects for collective global climate action. He believes the gathering of countries, organisations and campaigners at COP31 demonstrates a shared desire to secure a cleaner and more sustainable environment for present and future generations. As he continues to pedal for climate awareness, his message remains is that meaningful environmental action requires individual commitment, collective responsibility and opportunities for young people to shape the future they want to see.

items.title: Le football guinéen en deuil : Petit Sory Keïta, légende du Hafia FC, est décédé
items.description: Le football guinéen est en deuil. Petit Sory Keïta, ancien ailier droit du Hafia FC et figure emblématique de l’épopée du club vert et blanc, est décédé ce samedi 21 novembre à Conakry, des suites de maladie. Virevoltant ailier droit, Petit Sory Keïta a marqué l’histoire du Hafia FC, qu’il a porté de 1965 à 1981. Durant cette période, il s’est imposé comme l’un des acteurs majeurs de la grande génération du club, qui a fait rayonner le football guinéen sur le continent africain. Son nom restera à jamais associé aux grandes heures du Hafia FC, triple vainqueur de la Coupe d’Afrique des clubs champions en 1972, 1975 et 1977. Une épopée historique à laquelle l’ancien international guinéen a largement contribué, grâce à son talent, sa vivacité et sa capacité à faire la différence sur son couloir droit. Avec la disparition de Petit Sory Keïta, c’est une page importante de l’histoire du football guinéen qui se tourne. Son parcours et sa contribution aux succès du Hafia FC resteront gravés dans la mémoire des amoureux du ballon rond. Pour l’heure, aucun programme n’a été annoncé pour ses obsèques.
